docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

The Astros are great for most work, but not for offboard controls research. Their remotes drain fast, and a repair takes a year or more.

The Herelink Remotes Drain Very Quickly

The Astros' Herelink RC controllers drain their batteries very quickly. You still need one to fly or land safely when using offboard control. Charge it before every flight and watch its battery.

Never Update the Herelink Controllers

Do not update the software or the AMC version on the Herelink controllers. A newer version installed by mistake on astro2's remote caused a poor radio connection, apps that no longer work, and parameters with new limits, and it has not been fixed.

docs.title: Not Recommended for Offboard Controls Research
docs.text:
Do not use the Astros for offboard controls research (for example, an adaptive control paper), because:

  1. The onboard computer is weak.
  2. The telemetry rate cannot be raised above the default 30 Hz.
  3. The Chrony server cannot be used to monitor the health or age of the telemetry and the PX4 link.

The Astros are great for everything else. For controls experiments, use a Homebrew.

docs.title: Repairs Are Slow and Expensive
docs.text: The Astros are much more expensive to break than the Homebrews. Sending one to Freefly for repair takes about a year or more. See Repairs.

At a glance

How to point an Astro at our RTK corrections. The Astros use their NTRIP client app with the RTKLib caster.

RTK corrections make GPS position centimeter-level accurate, allowing much better precisse handling and repeatability of experiments. We require RTK to guarantee that altitude estimation is accurate enough to prevent collisions with the net. A ground station at a known position sends corrections to the robot, which uses them to remove the GPS error it shares with the ground station.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Written by Brandon Fallin, Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

The parameters to set on every Astro, and which are critical for safety. The PX4 wiki is not a reliable guide for them.

Check These Settings Before Every Flight

Before you take off the Astro, make sure the parameters in the table below are set as listed. In the Safety settings, also make sure that all RTL and takeoff altitudes are not greater than 2.5 m.

The PX4 Wiki Is Not an Accurate Guide for These Parameters

The Astros run an out-of-tree version of Auterion PX4 (APX4), which is itself a branch of PX4. Software stack v2.3.7 uses APX4 3.2.8 (v1.15.0-3.2.8-558-g98feccfbd6). Parameter names, ranges, and behavior can differ from the PX4 wiki. Trust this page, not the PX4 wiki.

docs.title: How to Change Parameters
docs.text:
There are three ways.

  1. Auterion Mission Control (AMC) on your computer. Download AMC from Auterion Suite. It is free, but you need to log in.
  2. The USB-C port. Connect to the Astro's USB-C port and set the parameters in the dashboard at https://10.41.1.1/. This is the equivalent of QGroundControl on the Homebrews.
  3. AMC on the Herelink controller. Tap the navigation arrow (menu) in the top left 7 times, then tap Switch to Advanced Mode. Parameters is then available under Advanced in the menu.

docs.title: Parameters to Set
docs.text:
Set every Astro to the values in the Set To column. astro1 and astro2 were checked on software v2.3.7. astro3 has not been checked.

Parameter Set To Notes BAT_CRIT_THR 0.4 BAT_EMERGEN_THR 0.3 COM_LOW_BAT_ACT 3 (Land mode) Critical. COM_ARM_GCS_REQ 1 (Enabled) Stops offboard programs from arming without the RC. Otherwise this is a safety issue. COM_RC_OVERRIDE 3 Needed so the RC can override offboard code and auto modes. NAV_RCL_ACT 3 (Land mode) EKF2_GPS_CTRL 7 Needed so the altitude estimate uses the RTK values, and so it is consistent across reboots with the code in aero_common. Otherwise the z-estimate is all over the place. This is not dangerous only because we use RTK. RTL_RETURN_ALT 2 Critical. Meters. RTL_DESCEND_ALT 2 Critical. Meters. COM_FLTMODE5 9 (Position Slow) Does not really matter. COM_GCS_SYS_ID Unknown FF_INPUT_TYPE 6 MC_SLOW_MAP_HVEL 0 Effect unknown. MC_SLOW_MAP_VVEL 0 Effect unknown. MC_SLOW_MAP_YAWR 0 Effect unknown. RC_MAP_AUX1 to RC_MAP_AUX4 0 Effect unknown. RC11_MAX to RC16_MAX 2000 RC11_MIN to RC16_MIN 1000 RC11_TRIM to RC16_TRIM 1500 EKF2_RNG_CTRL 1 (Enabled conditionally) Left at Freefly's default; helps with landing, but RTK makes it somewhat unnecessary. COM_OBL_RC_ACT Position Mode Drops you into Position Mode (thus holding in place) if the off-board heartbeat stops for COM_OF_LOSS_T seconds. TC_* Do not change Sensor calibration values, individual to each quadcopter.

Some Raw Values Are Missing

Max could not determine the raw value of every parameter above.

docs.text: Unlike upgrading PX4 on the Homebrews, flashing a new Freefly Astro software bundle (and so a new AuterionOS) gives you the set of parameters Freefly recommends. Stick to these, apart from the parameters in the table above. Freefly does not port your own parameters when you upgrade either, so write down any you change.

docs.title: Autonomy
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

A Docker container that runs MAVROS and the ZED ROS 2 wrapper on any Homebrew. Use it instead of installing them by hand.

Everything on this page runs on Linux.

Set Up the RTK Ground Station First

This robot uses RTK corrections from the ground station. Before you do anything else, set up the RTK ground station.

RTK Setup

What a Good Fix Is for a Quadcopter

A good fix is fix_type 6, always. Read the fix_type entry of <namespace>/mavros/gpsstatus/gps1/raw. When everything works, every single message coming out of MAVROS shows 6 (RTK fixed) while flying around, never less.

This reliability is only tested up to three quadcopters under the current setup: RTKLib on the discovery server computer. Three agents have also been tested with the Emlid RS3's embedded caster, which sends corrections over an individual link to every quadcopter (every local NTRIP client). That is not reliable at all: the fix drops out randomly and intermittently. Even with one agent, flying can reduce the fix to 5 from what it was on the ground, with no recovery and no explanation. Use the RTKLib caster, never the embedded caster.

Wait for the Fix to Reach 6

Getting a fix takes 5 to 15 minutes. Until fix_type reaches 6, expect lots of "Global position estimate invalid" errors. A fix of 5 (RTK float) can make flights unstable, so it is very important to wait for 6 (fixed) before you fly.

The fix should drop to 5 or lower, even for a single frame, only if you hit the ground hard, crash, or the satellites cut out. (The satellites cut out once in 100 flight hours.) Moving fast or changing altitude should never demote the fix.

Multi-agent testing has not been done, so it is unknown whether network traffic, or changing access points, affects the fix.

An Easier Way to Check the Fix

Click the GPS icon in the Fly tab of AMC (Astros) or QGC (Homebrews) to check the RTK fix.

We have developed a Docker container which allows you to run MAVROS and the Zed ROS2 Wrapper quickly and easily on any of the Homebrew drones.

We are using a slightly modified version of the Docker image found in the zed-ros2-wrapper. For a full install guide, see the README in the homebrew_docker repository.

docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy ParkIndoor Lab

At a glance

The Homebrews fly on 6S LiPo batteries. No one has counted them, and track each pack's cycles on its plastic sheet.

The Homebrews fly on 6S LiPo batteries, which we call the Homebrew batteries. No one has counted how many we have. Some are at the Autonomy Park and some are at the Indoor Lab.

Most of them should have a plastic sheet on them to help keep track of the number of cycles. Please use it whenever you can, to help track battery age.

docs.title: Calibration and Per-Drone Parameters
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-10-21Autonomy Park

At a glance

The PX4 parameters that are unique to each Homebrew and never copied between drones. Read it so you know what parameters should differ between drones.

Read Parameters in the PX4 v1.16 Reference Only

To understand any parameter on this page, use the PX4 v1.16 parameter reference. Do not use the main (latest) reference: parameters differ between PX4 versions.

The Taranis QX7 Is Max Gardenswartz's Personal Radio

The Taranis QX7 belongs to Max Gardenswartz personally, not to the lab, and he will not leave it with the lab when he graduates in 2028. He set it up for test flights because it was familiar and convenient. Research funds can only buy equipment that is on the Blue list, so the lab needs a better long-term plan: see Radio and RC Setup.

Reference: PX4 v1.16 (release/1.16). Values in the "Sample" column come from one sample drone. "Default" is the v1.16 source default.

These parameters are not part of the first-time setup checklist in PX4 Configuration. They are unique to each physical drone (sensor and battery calibrations, device IDs) or written by the firmware itself (see the last section). After a full parameter wipe or a firmware upgrade, redo the calibrations below on every drone. Do not copy another drone's values. Parameter names may change between firmware versions, so re-check the names against the new release.

docs.title: Unique to Each Drone: Redo on Every Quadcopter
Gyroscope (CAL_GYRO*)
docs.text:
Each quadcopter needs its own gyroscope calibration. The firmware also relearns and saves gyro offsets by itself over time, so these values drift slightly from boot to boot.

Parameter Name Sample Default Reason CAL_GYRO0_XOFF / YOFF / ZOFF −0.001093 / −0.004653 / 0.025502 0 Each quadcopter needs its own gyroscope calibration. CAL_GYRO1_XOFF / YOFF / ZOFF 0.017696 / −0.007145 / 0.004775 0 Same. CAL_GYRO2_XOFF / YOFF / ZOFF 0.034279 / 0.000794 / 0.000492 0 Same.

docs.title: Accelerometer (CAL_ACC*)
docs.text: Parameter Name Sample Default Reason CAL_ACC0_XOFF / YOFF / ZOFF, XSCALE / YSCALE / ZSCALE 0.134527 / 0.047541 / 0.039388, scales 1 / 1 / 1 0 offsets, 1 scales Each quadcopter needs its own accelerometer calibration. CAL_ACC1_* (same six) 0.273077 / −0.156760 / −0.185613, scales 1.002418 / 1.000138 / 0.988593 0 offsets, 1 scales Same. CAL_ACC2_* (same six) −0.024469 / 0.267408 / 0.261582, scales 1.003901 / 0.999136 / 0.987734 0 offsets, 1 scales Same.

docs.title: Compass (CAL_MAG*)
docs.text:
Calibration slots are matched to sensors by device ID (CAL_MAG*_ID), so the same compass can sit in a different slot on a different drone.

Parameter Name Sample Default Reason CAL_MAG0_XOFF / YOFF / ZOFF, XSCALE / YSCALE / ZSCALE 0.103816 / −0.113710 / 0.023709, scales 1.024196 / 0.997193 / 0.974344 0 offsets, 1 scales Each quadcopter needs its own compass calibration. CAL_MAG1_* (offsets, scales and XODIAG / YODIAG / ZODIAG) 0.123004 / −0.029632 / 0.013106, scales 0.972365 / 1.071113 / 0.946423, odiag −0.022899 / 0.006623 / 0.001966 0 offsets, 1 scales, 0 odiag Same.

docs.title: Barometer (CAL_BARO*_OFF)
docs.text: Parameter Name Sample Default Reason CAL_BARO1_OFF 87.328125 0 Written by the firmware for this specific sensor. Not copied between drones.

docs.title: Level Flight (SENS_BOARD_X_OFF, SENS_BOARD_Y_OFF)
docs.text:
These are the parameters QGC's Level Horizon (Level Flight) calibration writes. In the PX4 source, level_calibration.cpp updates exactly these two: roll offset to SENS_BOARD_X_OFF and pitch offset to SENS_BOARD_Y_OFF, in degrees. SENS_BOARD_Z_OFF (yaw) is not touched by that calibration and stays 0.

Parameter Name Sample Default Reason SENS_BOARD_X_OFF −2.0350902° 0 Each quadcopter needs its own Level Flight calibration. SENS_BOARD_Y_OFF −0.3200225° 0 Same.

docs.title: RC Calibration (RC1 to RC10)
docs.text:
Max manually calibrated the RC to trim away stick drift for his personal Taranis QX7. Defaults are 1000 (min), 1500 (trim), 2000 (max).

Parameter Name Sample (MIN / TRIM / MAX) Default Reason RC1_MIN / RC1_TRIM / RC1_MAX 982 / 1492 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Manually calibrated RC to trim away stick drift. RC2_* 982 / 1494 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. RC3_* 982 / 982 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. (Throttle trim sits at minimum.) RC4_* 982 / 1497 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. RC5_* 1150 / 1578 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. RC6_* 982 / 1494 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. RC7_* 982 / 1494 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. RC8_* 982 / 1494 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. RC9_* 982 / 1494 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same. RC10_* 982 / 1494 / 2006 1000 / 1500 / 2000 Same.

docs.title: Battery Sensing (BAT1_V_DIV, BAT1_A_PER_V)
docs.text:
Each quadcopter needs its own battery voltage-divider and current-per-volt calibration. In v1.16 the metadata default for both is −1, which means "use the board default"; the Cube Orange board defaults are 10.1 and 17. The other battery parameters are in Homebrew Parameters.

Parameter Name Sample Default Reason BAT1_V_DIV 12.05901 −1 (uses the Cube Orange board default, 10.1) Found by a unique calibration for each quadcopter. BAT1_A_PER_V 6.940631 −1 (uses the Cube Orange board default, 17) Found by a unique calibration for each quadcopter.

docs.title: Sensor Device IDs and Priorities (CAL_*_ID, CAL_*_PRIO, CAL_MAG0_ROT)
docs.text:
Each calibration slot above is tied to a sensor through its device ID. The ID encodes the bus type, bus, address and device type, so the same sensor can land in a different slot on a different drone. Sample IDs are from one drone; treat them as per-drone values and do not copy them. Which of these the firmware writes automatically when it detects or calibrates a sensor has not been verified in the source.

Parameter Name Sample Default Reason CAL_ACC0_ID / CAL_ACC1_ID / CAL_ACC2_ID 3670050 / 2621474 / 2424842 0 Device IDs of the three accelerometers. Per drone. CAL_ACC0_PRIO / CAL_ACC1_PRIO / CAL_ACC2_PRIO 50 / 50 / 50 −1 (uninitialized) 50 is "Medium (Default)" in the parameter enum. CAL_GYRO0_ID / CAL_GYRO1_ID / CAL_GYRO2_ID 3670050 / 2621474 / 2424842 0 Device IDs of the three gyroscopes. Per drone. CAL_GYRO0_PRIO / CAL_GYRO1_PRIO / CAL_GYRO2_PRIO 50 / 50 / 50 −1 (uninitialized) Same. CAL_MAG0_ID / CAL_MAG1_ID 8944643 / 589858 0 Device IDs of the two compasses. Per drone. CAL_MAG0_PRIO / CAL_MAG1_PRIO 75 / 0 −1 (uninitialized) 75 is "High" and 0 is "Disabled" in the parameter enum. CAL_MAG0_ROT 0 −1 (Internal) 0 is "No rotation" in the parameter enum. CAL_MAG1_ROT was at the default (−1). CAL_BARO0_ID / CAL_BARO1_ID 3997730 / 3997706 0 Device IDs of the two barometers. Per drone. CAL_BARO0_PRIO / CAL_BARO1_PRIO 50 / 50 −1 (uninitialized) Same as the accelerometers.

docs.title: Written by the Firmware: Do Not Set
docs.text:
These are written by PX4 itself while it runs. Do not set them by hand and do not copy them from another drone. They are listed so that a full parameter comparison does not flag them as mistakes. In the v1.16 source, the QGC "reset all" task and the boot-time reset both keep LND_FLIGHT_T_HI, LND_FLIGHT_T_LO and COM_FLIGHT_UUID; EKF2_MAG_DECL is not excluded and returns to its default.

Parameter Name Sample Default What writes it LND_FLIGHT_T_HI / LND_FLIGHT_T_LO 1 / 795910513 0 / 0 Total flight time of this autopilot in microseconds, (HI << 32) \| LO. Written by the land detector (LandDetector.cpp). Unique to each quadcopter. COM_FLIGHT_UUID 25 0 Number of the next flight, incremented automatically on every disarm. Written by the commander (Commander.cpp). Unique to each quadcopter. EKF2_MAG_DECL −6.299414° 0 Magnetic declination. The estimator stores the declination it learns when it differs from the stored value by more than 0.1° (EKF2.cpp), so it changes with where in the world the drone is flown.

docs.title: Flying Manually
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

How to fly a Homebrew manually: pre-flight, the transmitter's switches, takeoff, in-flight conduct, and landing. Read the warnings first.

This Guide Is for Max Gardenswartz's Personal Radio

This guide is for Max Gardenswartz's personal radio (a Taranis QX7). It is not a long-term solution for the lab. After Max graduates, flying manually will need to be set up again from scratch.

New to flying? Practice in a simulator first.

Quadcopter Flight Practice

Set Up the RTK Ground Station First

This robot uses RTK corrections from the ground station. Before you do anything else, set up the RTK ground station.

RTK Setup

What a Good Fix Is for a Quadcopter

A good fix is fix_type 6, always. Read the fix_type entry of <namespace>/mavros/gpsstatus/gps1/raw. When everything works, every single message coming out of MAVROS shows 6 (RTK fixed) while flying around, never less.

This reliability is only tested up to three quadcopters under the current setup: RTKLib on the discovery server computer. Three agents have also been tested with the Emlid RS3's embedded caster, which sends corrections over an individual link to every quadcopter (every local NTRIP client). That is not reliable at all: the fix drops out randomly and intermittently. Even with one agent, flying can reduce the fix to 5 from what it was on the ground, with no recovery and no explanation. Use the RTKLib caster, never the embedded caster.

Wait for the Fix to Reach 6

Getting a fix takes 5 to 15 minutes. Until fix_type reaches 6, expect lots of "Global position estimate invalid" errors. A fix of 5 (RTK float) can make flights unstable, so it is very important to wait for 6 (fixed) before you fly.

The fix should drop to 5 or lower, even for a single frame, only if you hit the ground hard, crash, or the satellites cut out. (The satellites cut out once in 100 flight hours.) Moving fast or changing altitude should never demote the fix.

Multi-agent testing has not been done, so it is unknown whether network traffic, or changing access points, affects the fix.

An Easier Way to Check the Fix

Click the GPS icon in the Fly tab of AMC (Astros) or QGC (Homebrews) to check the RTK fix.

Never Fly in Acro Mode

Acro Mode must never be attempted, under any circumstances.

Flying in Stabilized Mode requires expertise. Novice pilots must not attempt it.

Position Mode is already quite fast. Be very careful and move the sticks very slowly.

Keep the Optical Flow and Lidar Clear

Make sure no cables are in the way of the optical flow sensor or the lidar. Make sure the lidar's position does not obscure the optical flow sensor: they are close to each other.

Always Watch the Battery

The pilot must always watch the battery while flying. Conservative failsafes stop you from flying on a low battery, but they do not replace watching it.

Leaving a drone plugged in for a long time (for example 3 hours) does not prevent the battery from draining slowly. You can easily draw a LiPo below its safe limit of 3.0 V per cell. This permanently damages the battery, and PX4 gives no warning at all.

The Taranis QX7 Is Max Gardenswartz's Personal Radio

The Taranis QX7 belongs to Max Gardenswartz personally, not to the lab, and he will not leave it with the lab when he graduates in 2028. He set it up for test flights because it was familiar and convenient. Research funds can only buy equipment that is on the Blue list, so the lab needs a better long-term plan: see Radio and RC Setup.

docs.title: Control Mapping
docs.text: Channel Input Function 1 Right Stick (X) Roll 2 Right Stick (Y) Pitch 3 Left Stick (Y) Throttle 4 Left Stick (X) Yaw 5 Switch A (SA) Mode Logic (Primary) 6 Switch B (SB) Mode Logic (Secondary) 9 Switch F (SF) Arm / Disarm (2-Position) 10 Switch H (SH) Return to Launch (RTL)

docs.title: PX4 Flight Mode Logic
docs.text: SA Position SB Position Resulting Flight Mode Up / Middle Up Position (GPS Horizontal Hold) Up / Middle Middle Hold (GPS Loiter) Up / Middle Down Land (Automatic Descent) Down Up Altitude (Baro/Z-axis Hold only) Down Middle Altitude (Baro/Z-axis Hold only) Down Down Stabilized (Full Manual / Self-Level)

docs.title: Takeoff Loop (The "30-50-70" Rule)
docs.text:
1. Mode Select: Before arming, put the remote in Position Mode (SA Up, SB Up), or whichever mode you intend to fly in. Do not arm in Stabilized Mode.
  2. Arm: Flick Switch F up. (It should start down.)
  3. Launch: Within 5 seconds, bring the throttle to 30-50%.
  4. Hover: Increase throttle to ~70% (Hover).
  5. Note: Position Mode holds both position and altitude when the sticks are centered. See the PX4 v1.16 multicopter flight modes.

docs.title: In-Flight Conduct
docs.text:
• No Acrobatics: These are research platforms, not racing drones. No flips, rolls, or high-speed maneuvers.
  • Stay in Mode: Once armed, it is very dangerous to switch flight modes. The only exceptions are Land and Hold. The sudden change in GPS dependency can cause instability that is difficult to recover from.
  • Remote Safety: Never set the remote on the ground or a chair while the drone is live. The Arm switch (SF) is easily bumped by clothing.

docs.title: Landing Procedure
docs.text:
1. Maintain Mode: Stay in your current flight mode (Position mode is acceptable for landing).
  2. Slow Descent: Ease the throttle down as slowly as possible.
  3. The Ground Effect: As you approach the floor, an air cushion (Ground Effect) will make the drone "float." You will need to slowly decrease throttle further to punch through this cushion for touchdown.
  4. Disarm: Once the landing gear makes contact, flick Switch F (SF) to the Down position.
  5. Safety Buffer: Wait for the motors to come to a complete stop before entering the net.

Warning: In the current PX4 configuration, the disarm switch is not a "Kill Switch." If flipped in the air, the drone will attempt to land rather than cutting power immediately.

docs.title: Position Mode Should Hold Position
docs.text:
With the sticks centered, a Homebrew in Position Mode holds its position and altitude indefinitely without drifting. The PX4 v1.16 documentation describes all the multicopter flight modes: Flight Modes (Multicopter).

  • With RTK: unbounded drift, or drift of more than 0.5 to 1 m vertically or horizontally, is not normal.
  • Without RTK: expect to hold within about 1.5 m vertically and 1 m horizontally, and no worse.

If the quadcopter drifts more than this, land and check the fix: see RTK Setup.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

Half of the Homebrews have bad lidar cables, battery readings are voltage-only and sag, and nothing turns off a low-battery Homebrew that is not armed.

Nothing Turns Off a Low-Battery Homebrew That Is Not Armed

If a Homebrew is on but not armed, nothing shuts it off when the battery runs low. You are responsible for watching its battery in QGC and unplugging it, especially if debugging takes hours.

Half of the Homebrews Have Bad Lidar Cables

Half of the Homebrews' lidars were soldered with a custom cable that proved devastating to safe flight. See the status table below for which ones, and Case Study: Lidar and CAN Sensor Burnout.

docs.title: The Homebrew SD Cards Are Slow
docs.text: The Homebrews' SD cards have a very slow write speed, at most 5 MB/s. Logging anything more than SDLOG_PROFILE = 1 to the SD card causes gaps in the data. Faster SD cards are expensive, so this is not planned to change.

docs.title: The Landing Gear Retracts on Landing If Plugged In
docs.text: If the landing gear is plugged in, it retracts on landing. It is probably fixable, but we just unplugged it.

docs.title: Battery Readings Are Voltage-Only
docs.text: The current sensor is either not soldered or not configured correctly (most likely not soldered). All battery level measurements are therefore voltage-only, and voltage sags under load. Set the battery thresholds conservatively for safety. See Parameters.

docs.title: Microhard Radios
docs.text:
Draft. Future work. Not installed on any Homebrew yet. Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-03Autonomy Park

At a glance

Microhard radios are the planned data link for multi-agent flights with the Homebrews. This page is mostly blank until the first one is installed.

Not Installed Yet

Nothing on this page has been done on a Homebrew yet.

A wireless LAN can be problematic with many agents, and it is untested at present. Microhard radios are the way to go. We have one for each Homebrew. They connect to the Jetson on each Homebrew over USB.

docs.title: What Is Needed
docs.text:
Each radio needs an additional voltage regulator soldered to the PDB. This needs some disassembly of the quadcopter. Test the work on one Homebrew before doing more.

The steps, the radio models, and how many we have: Unknown.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Written by Brandon Fallin, Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

Quick facts about the Homebrew: physical measurements, manuals, and video guides. Look here when you need a number or a manual.

A Homebrew.

Bill of Materials

Set Up the RTK Ground Station First

This robot uses RTK corrections from the ground station. Before you do anything else, set up the RTK ground station.

RTK Setup

Wait for a Full RTK Fix Before You Fly

Wait until the RTK fix is full (fix_type 6, RTK fixed), not 5 (RTK float), before you fly. Getting a fix takes 5 to 15 minutes.

Never Fly in Acro Mode

Acro Mode must never be attempted, under any circumstances.

Flying in Stabilized Mode requires expertise. Novice pilots must not attempt it.

Position Mode is already quite fast. Be very careful and move the sticks very slowly.

Keep the Optical Flow and Lidar Clear

Make sure no cables are in the way of the optical flow sensor or the lidar. Make sure the lidar's position does not obscure the optical flow sensor: they are close to each other.

Always Watch the Battery

The pilot must always watch the battery while flying. Conservative failsafes stop you from flying on a low battery, but they do not replace watching it.

Leaving a drone plugged in for a long time (for example 3 hours) does not prevent the battery from draining slowly. You can easily draw a LiPo below its safe limit of 3.0 V per cell. This permanently damages the battery, and PX4 gives no warning at all.

Never Power On a Wrongly Wired Lidar

Never power on a lidar that is wired with the custom connector instead of the cable included in the box. Doing so slowly burns out the lidar over time.

Lidars 02, 03, and 04 are likely burned out. They no longer have their original cables, so they cannot be tested. Whether the original cables can be soldered back without further intermittent issues is unknown. We recommend never plugging them in again.

Attaching a Payload

Disable EKF2_OF_CTRL and EKF2_RNG_CTRL if you attach a payload. Move slowly. Do not attach more than 1 kg: this is the tested safe limit.

For controls experiments, consider also disabling MPC_USE_HTE and manually tuning MPC_THR_HOVER (not to exceed 0.7). See Parameters.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

Every PX4 parameter the Homebrew template sets, what it is set to, and why. Use it with the PX4 v1.16 reference only.

Read Parameters in the PX4 v1.16 Reference Only

To understand any parameter on this page, use the PX4 v1.16 parameter reference. Do not use the main (latest) reference: parameters differ between PX4 versions.

The Taranis QX7 Is Max Gardenswartz's Personal Radio

The Taranis QX7 belongs to Max Gardenswartz personally, not to the lab, and he will not leave it with the lab when he graduates in 2028. He set it up for test flights because it was familiar and convenient. Research funds can only buy equipment that is on the Blue list, so the lab needs a better long-term plan: see Radio and RC Setup.

The Homebrews' SD cards are slow: see Known Issues.

Warning

Before you take off the Homebrew, make sure the following settings are correct.

Reference: PX4 v1.16 parameter definitions (release/1.16; entries added later were checked against the v1.16.2 tag). "Default" means the v1.16 metadata default plus the CubePilot Cube Orange board defaults (rc.board_defaults), the multicopter defaults in rc.mc_defaults (which overrides RTL_RETURN_ALT and RTL_DESCEND_ALT and sets MAV_TYPE), and the Generic Quadcopter airframe defaults (4001_quad_x, which sets the CA_ROTOR* positions).

Legend: ✅ = matches the multicopter default, ❌ = differs from the multicopter default.

The Relevance column in every table tells you which descriptions are most important to read: High means read the Reason before you change or rely on the parameter, and "-" means it is rarely worth your time.

docs.title: BAT: Battery
docs.text:
Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason BAT1_CAPACITY -1 Disabled ✅ - Default −1 (unknown). Left disabled so remaining charge is estimated from voltage only. The current sensor is not working, so coulomb counting would integrate invalid current. Set to 16000 mAh (all Homebrew batteries) once current sensing is verified. BAT1_I_OVERWRITE 0 A Idle-current overwrite disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled, the measured current is used). BAT1_N_CELLS 6 6S battery ❌ - Default 0 (unknown). Should be set by the user to match the battery. BAT1_R_INTERNAL −1 Ω Use the online estimate ✅ - Default −1 (use the online estimate). Left at default because the current sensor is not working, and both the sag compensation and the online estimate need valid current. The PX4 parameter description says this is per cell. BAT1_SOURCE 0 Battery 1 read from the power module ✅ - Default 0 (Power Module). The other options are 1 (External, from MAVLink battery status messages) and 2 (ESCs, taken from the esc_status message, which per the v1.16.2 description requires the ESCs to report both voltage and current). PX4 currently cannot read the current from the PDB. Max thinks setting this to 2 might fix that, but this is not verified, and since the notes for COM_ARM_CHK_ESCS say these ESCs do not support telemetry, it may not be possible at all. Requires reboot. BAT1_V_CHARGED 4.05 V 4.05 V per cell when full ✅ High Default 4.05 V. The PX4 LiPo default, defined as the per-cell voltage under load rather than the resting full-charge voltage. BAT1_V_EMPTY 3.6 V 3.6 V per cell when empty ✅ - Default 3.6 V. The PX4 LiPo default, defined as the per-cell voltage under load when the pack is effectively empty. BAT2_A_PER_V 17 Battery 2 current scale at board default ✅ - Default 17 (Cube Orange board default). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_CAPACITY −1 mAh Battery 2 capacity unknown ✅ - Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_I_CHANNEL −1 Battery 2 current ADC channel at board default ✅ - Default −1 (board default). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_I_OVERWRITE 0 A Idle-current overwrite disabled ✅ - Default 0. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_N_CELLS 0 Cell count unknown ✅ - Default 0. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_R_INTERNAL −1 Ω Use the online estimate ✅ - Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_SOURCE −1 Battery 2 disabled ✅ - Default −1 (Disabled). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_CHANNEL −1 Battery 2 voltage ADC channel at board default ✅ - Default −1 (board default). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_CHARGED 4.05 V 4.05 V per cell when full ✅ - Default 4.05 V. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_DIV 10.1 Battery 2 voltage divider at board default ✅ - Default 10.1 (Cube Orange board default). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_EMPTY 3.6 V 3.6 V per cell when empty ✅ - Default 3.6 V. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT3_CAPACITY −1 mAh Battery 3 capacity unknown ✅ - Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_N_CELLS 0 Cell count unknown ✅ - Default 0. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_R_INTERNAL −1 Ω Use the online estimate ✅ - Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_SOURCE −1 Battery 3 disabled ✅ - Default −1 (Disabled). Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_V_CHARGED 4.05 V 4.05 V per cell when full ✅ - Default 4.05 V. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_V_EMPTY 3.6 V 3.6 V per cell when empty ✅ - Default 3.6 V. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT_AVRG_CURRENT 15 A 15 A expected in-flight current ✅ - Default 15 A. Only used to initialize the in-flight average-current estimate, which feeds remaining-flight-time and RTL triggering. BAT_CRIT_THR 0.25 Critical at 25% remaining ❌ High Default 0.07. Triggers the critical-battery reaction (land) much earlier, so the Homebrew lands with a healthy reserve (about 3.71 V per cell with the linear 3.6–4.05 V mapping). Must stay below BAT_LOW_THR and above BAT_EMERGEN_THR. Units are normalized 0–1, not percent. BAT_EMERGEN_THR 0.15 Emergency at 15% remaining ❌ High Default 0.05. Immediate-landing level (about 3.67 V per cell). Must stay below BAT_CRIT_THR. BAT_LOW_THR 0.35 Low at 35% remaining ❌ High Default 0.15. First warning level (about 3.76 V per cell). Must stay above BAT_CRIT_THR.

Note that BAT1_V_DIV and BAT1_A_PER_V are calibrated separately for every quadcopter!

In v1.16.2 only batteries 1 and 2 have BAT*_V_DIV, BAT*_A_PER_V, BAT*_V_CHANNEL, BAT*_I_CHANNEL and BAT*_I_OVERWRITE, so those parameters do not exist for battery 3; only the six BAT3_* parameters above do.

docs.title: CA: Control Allocator
docs.text:
Positions are along the body X and Y axes, in metres, relative to the center of gravity. They describe the physical span of the airframe and are critical to the motor mixer and flight stability. The Generic Quadcopter airframe (4001_quad_x) sets them to ±1 m. The metadata default is 0.

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason CA_ROTOR0_PX 0.25 m Rotor 0 at +0.25 m on X ❌ - Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR0_PY 0.25 m Rotor 0 at +0.25 m on Y ❌ - Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR1_PX −0.25 m Rotor 1 at −0.25 m on X ❌ - Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR1_PY −0.25 m Rotor 1 at −0.25 m on Y ❌ - Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR2_PX 0.25 m Rotor 2 at +0.25 m on X ❌ - Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR2_PY −0.25 m Rotor 2 at −0.25 m on Y ❌ - Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR3_PX −0.25 m Rotor 3 at −0.25 m on X ❌ - Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR3_PY 0.25 m Rotor 3 at +0.25 m on Y ❌ - Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe.

docs.title: COM: Commander
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason COM_ACT_FAIL_ACT 0 Warning only on actuator failure ✅ - Default 0 (warning only). The action taken when the failure detector reports a failed actuator (motor); the other options are 1 Hold, 2 Land, 3 Return, and 4 Terminate. It only matters if the actuator failure check is enabled and configured through the FD_ACT_* parameters (see the FD section). Max is unsure whether this should be changed to Land (2) since the current sensor is not working, but he uses 0 and it has been fine. COM_ARM_AUTH_MET 0 One-step arming ✅ - Default 0 (one arm: request authorization and arm as soon as it is received). The alternative is 1 (two-step arm: the first arm command requests authorization and the second arms if it is authorized). It is only used when COM_ARM_AUTH_REQ is on, so it has no effect here. COM_ARM_AUTH_REQ 0 No arm authorization required ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). No authorization is required to arm other than the arm switch. COM_ARM_BAT_MIN 0.50 Refuse to arm below 50% battery ❌ High Default −1 (uses BAT_CRIT_THR). Prevents permanently damaging the battery through negligence. COM_ARM_CHK_ESCS 0 ESC arming checks disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). Enables checks of the ESCs' online status and failures. It is specific to ESCs that report telemetry and must only be enabled if the ESCs support it; these ESCs do not. COM_ARM_HFLT_CHK 0 Disabled; allow arming even if hardfault files are on the SD card ❌ High Default 1 (enabled). The CubePilot Orange+ (a flight controller similar to our CubePilot Blue) has a bug in PX4 1.16.2, PX4 issue #29346: disconnecting from USB causes a hard fault, leaving a log that prevents arming. That is easy to do by accident and is not a problem, so it should not prevent arming. Enabling the check means the failed USB connection prevents all further arming until you delete the logs from SD (via the NuttX terminal or taking the SD card out). Leave it off until the bug is patched (likely PX4 1.19). COM_ARM_MAG_STR 1 Deny arming on a magnetic disturbance ❌ - Default 2 (warning only). Controls what happens when the estimator detects a strong magnetic disturbance, as checked according to EKF2_MAG_CHECK: 0 disabled, 1 deny arming, 2 warning only. Denying arming, not just warning, keeps a vehicle with a disturbed magnetometer on the ground. COM_ARM_SDCARD 2 No SD prevents arming ❌ - Default 1 (warning only). No SD card detected despite on in the quad (which should be the case) means the FC might damage, so this is reasonable proxy. SD card might also have burnt out from too many read-writes. This is natural and can happen with time. COM_ARM_WO_GPS 0 Deny arming when the GPS checks fail ❌ High Default 1 (warning only). For an autonomous quadcopter, having no usable GPS should stop it from moving forward. These drones only ever fly outdoors. In the v1.16 source, 0 denies arming when a check in EKF2_GPS_CHECK fails, and it also requires a global position estimate ("Global position estimate required"), which is why EKF2_HGT_REF must stay 1. With EKF2_GPS_CHECK = 1023 the default thresholds apply (EKF2_REQ_NSATS 6, EKF2_REQ_PDOP 2.5, EKF2_REQ_EPH 3 m, EKF2_REQ_EPV 5 m), so a poor fix (for example without RTK) can block arming. COM_ARMABLE 1 Arming allowed ✅ - Default 1 (arming allowed). Set it to 0 to prevent arming entirely, for example for safety or maintenance reasons, so the vehicle cannot be used by accident. COM_DISARM_LAND 2.0 s 2.0 s of successful landing detected ✅ - Default 2.0 s. PX4 must detect that the vehicle is on the ground for this long before disarming the motors at the end of Land mode procedure. COM_DISARM_MAN 1 Manual disarm allowed in manual thrust modes ✅ - Default 1 (enabled). Allows disarming with the switch, stick, or button during multicopter flight, but only in modes where the throttle stick directly controls thrust (for example Stabilized or Acro). With 0, disarming is not allowed unless the vehicle has landed. Disarming in flight kills the motors. COM_DISARM_PRFLT 10 s Disarm after 10 s without takeoff ✅ - Default 10 s. If the vehicle is armed and has not taken off within this time, it disarms again (a negative value disables this). The user has 10 s to act after arming. COM_DL_LOSS_T 5 s GCS connection counted as lost after 5 s ❌ - Default 10 s. Tighter is better, and 10 s is too generous, especially for an autonomous quadcopter. Because NAV_DLL_ACT is set as 0 later, this value is ignored, but it's good to have. COM_FAIL_ACT_T 5 s Wait 5 s in Hold before a failsafe action ✅ - Default 5 s. Before a failsafe action (Return, Land, or Hold) is executed, PX4 first waits this long in Hold mode so the user can realize something is wrong. During that time the pilot cannot take over with the stick override (COM_RC_OVERRIDE), although switching modes is still allowed; afterwards the configured action runs and the stick override works again. A value of 0 removes the delay. From the description it applies to the failsafes that are active here, such as RC loss (NAV_RCL_ACT) and offboard loss (COM_OBL_RC_ACT); the GCS-loss failsafe is disabled (NAV_DLL_ACT = 0), so it never starts this wait (my reading of the description; not tested). COM_FLT_TIME_MAX −1 s No maximum flight time ✅ - Default −1 (disabled). When set, the vehicle aborts the current operation and returns to launch once the time since takeoff exceeds this value, with a warning every minute starting at 90 % of it. No maximum flight time is used; the battery thresholds limit the flight time instead. COM_FLTMODE1 2 Slot 1: Position ❌ - Default −1 (unassigned). Necessary for using the Taranis QX7 remote specifically. With RC_MAP_FLTMODE the mode is picked by the range channel 5 is in, across six slots. A different RC would need a different scheme. COM_FLTMODE2 1 Slot 2: Altitude ❌ - Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTMODE3 4 Slot 3: Hold ❌ - Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTMODE4 1 Slot 4: Altitude ❌ - Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. Slots 2 and 4 are both Altitude. COM_FLTMODE5 11 Slot 5: Land ❌ - Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTMODE6 8 Slot 6: Stabilized ❌ - Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTT_LOW_ACT 3 Return when remaining flight time is low ✅ - Default 3 (Return). The action taken when the estimated remaining flight time drops below the time needed to reach the RTL destination (0 None, 1 Warning, 3 Return). It should hardly ever matter since the Park is so small. What is critical is that the return heights stay below the net, which is covered by RTL_RETURN_ALT and RTL_DESCEND_ALT. COM_HOME_EN 1 Home position set automatically ✅ - Default 1 (enabled). PX4 sets the home position automatically when possible (per Max, on arm or boot). Requires reboot. Home cannot be reset without arming, which is one reason the geofence altitude limit is not used (see GF_MAX_VER_DIST). COM_HOME_IN_AIR 0 Home is never set in the air ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). If enabled, the autopilot may set its home position after takeoff (back-computed from the local position when one is available). Disabled so that home is never set while flying. COM_IMB_PROP_ACT 0 Warning only on imbalanced propeller ✅ - Default 0 (warning only). The action taken when the failure detector detects an imbalanced propeller (−1 disabled, 0 warning, 1 Return, 2 Land). The detection threshold is FD_IMB_PROP_THR (default 30; 0 disables the detection). No motivation to change. COM_KILL_DISARM 0 s Kill switch disarms immediately ❌ - Default 5 s. Kill activates immediately with no timeout. Be careful!!! COM_LOW_BAT_ACT 2 Land mode ❌ - Default 0 (Warning only). Land instead of just warning at critical battery. COM_OBC_LOSS_T 5 s Companion computer loss warning after 5 s ✅ - Default 5 s. Time without a connection to the onboard computer after which PX4 only issues a warning; it is not a failsafe. No motivation to change: the round-trip time over MAVROS and the age of the odometry matter much more, and those have to be checked by the offboard code, not by PX4. COM_OBL_RC_ACT 4 Land mode (on offboard loss) ❌ - Default 0 (Position mode). Note: this is the offboard-loss action, not RC loss (see NAV_RCL_ACT). COM_OF_LOSS_T 0.5 0.5 s offboard-loss timeout ❌ - Default 1.0 s. Lowering makes crashes less likely during offboard network dropouts since the failsafe triggers faster. Too low may make this sensitive to network lag, but lower than 0.5 should be tested for feasibility. COM_POS_FS_EPH 5 m Failsafe above 5 m horizontal position error ✅ - Default 5 m (−1 disables). The horizontal position error (EPH) above which PX4 triggers a failsafe; once the error has been below the threshold, a factor of 2.5 is applied before the position is invalidated. Kept at default because the offboard code should land, or refuse to arm, whenever the GPS fix type is not 6 (RTK fixed), long before PX4's own failsafe matters. COM_POS_LOW_ACT 5 Land on a low position accuracy ❌ - Default 3 (Return). The action taken when the position accuracy is worse than the COM_POS_LOW_EPH threshold (0 None, 1 Warning, 2 Hold, 3 Return, 4 Terminate, 5 Land). Set to Land so that a poor position estimate lands the vehicle instead of returning it. Per the v1.16.2 description the action is only executed in Mission or Hold (loiter) modes, and otherwise it is only a warning; while COM_POS_LOW_EPH is disabled it has no effect at all. COM_POS_LOW_EPH −1 m Low accuracy failsafe disabled ✅ - Default −1 (disabled). Threshold for COM_POS_LOW_ACT. The local position must still be valid for it to apply, which requires some velocity aiding or a large dead-reckoning time (EKF2_NOAID_TOUT), together with a high COM_POS_FS_EPH. No motivation to change. COM_POSCTL_NAVL 1 Land when navigation is lost in Position mode ❌ High Default 0 (Altitude mode). The flight mode used when the navigation accuracy is no longer adequate for position control in manual Position mode: 0 Altitude mode, 1 Land mode (descend). This should never happen with RTK, but if the GPS is bad the vehicle lands. COM_PREARM_MODE 0 Prearm state disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). The prearmed state is an intermediate state between disarmed and armed in which non-throttling actuators are active; the options are 0 disabled, 1 safety button, 2 always. The prearm feature is not used here. COM_RC_IN_MODE 3 RC or Joystick, keep first ✅ - Default is 3 in v1.16. COM_RC_LOSS_T 0.5 s RC counted as lost after 0.5 s without input ✅ - Default 0.5 s. Time without a new setpoint from the RC or a joystick after which the connection is considered lost. It must be short, because the vehicle keeps using the last supplied setpoint until the timeout triggers. COM_RC_OVERRIDE 3 Stick override in auto and offboard modes ❌ High Default 1 (auto modes only). Bit 0 = auto, bit 1 = offboard. COM_RC_STICK_OV 30 % Stick movement past 30 % hands control to the pilot ✅ - Default 30 %. The threshold for COM_RC_OVERRIDE: when the sticks move more than this, PX4 gives control back to the pilot in Position mode. As I read ManualControl.cpp, it is compared against how fast a stick moves. Reasonable as is, but Max reports that it is reworked in PX4 1.18 (not verified by me), so re-check its name and meaning after upgrading to 1.18. COM_RCL_EXCEPT 7 Offboard, Mission, and Hold modes ❌ - Default 0 (no exceptions). Bitmask to specify where to ignore RC loss and not trigger the RC loss failsafe specified in NAV_RCL_ACT. 7 means RC is optional in Offboard, Mission, and Hold modes. Required for multi-agent setups since we only have one RC, but consider reverting to default when testing single-agent; RC then becomes required again. COM_SPOOLUP_TIME 1.0 s 1.0 s spool-up after arming ✅ - Default 1.0 s. The minimum time from arming the motors until the vehicle can be moved: the motors and propellers spool up to idle before being commanded faster, and the ESCs and smart batteries have time for their failure checks. Commands to move the vehicle are not applied until this time has passed after arming. No motivation to change. COM_TAKEOFF_ACT 0 Hold mode ✅ - Default 0 (Hold mode). Mode to change into after successful takeoff. Not much flexibility here, so this is why global position estimates are needed as explained in the reasoning for EKF2_HGT_REF. COM_VEL_FS_EVH 1 m/s Failsafe above 1 m/s horizontal velocity error ✅ - Default 1 m/s. The horizontal velocity error (EVH) above which PX4 triggers a failsafe, with the same factor of 2.5 between validating and invalidating as COM_POS_FS_EPH. No motivation to change. COM_WIND_MAX −1 m/s High wind failsafe disabled ✅ - Default −1 (disabled). The estimated wind speed above which the action in COM_WIND_MAX_ACT is triggered. No motivation to change; just do not fly in wind. COM_WIND_MAX_ACT 0 No high wind action ✅ - Default 0 (None). The action taken at COM_WIND_MAX (1 Warning, 2 Hold, 3 Return, 4 Terminate, 5 Land). No motivation to change. COM_WIND_WARN −1 m/s Wind warning disabled ✅ - Default −1 (disabled). When enabled, a warning is sent every minute while the estimated wind speed is above this value. No motivation to change.

docs.title: EKF2: Estimator
docs.text:
The EKF2_*_POS_* offsets (GPS, IMU, optical flow, rangefinder, external vision) are in the FRD body frame, measured from the center of gravity (CG): X is forward, Y is right, and Z is down. A sensor above the CG therefore has a negative Z.

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason EKF2_EV_CTRL 0 External vision fusion disabled ✅ - Default 0. Only relevant if a motion-capture system outdoors or a computer-vision camera aids the position estimate. This quad and workspace has neither. The sample drone had 15 (all four bits: horizontal position, vertical position, 3D velocity, yaw); Max is surprised by that and does not know who set it. Per the v1.16 source this is not limited to mocap or cameras: it applies to any vision/odometry input PX4 receives (for example MAVLink VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE or ODOMETRY, which a companion computer could send). EKF2_EV_DELAY 0 ms No external vision delay ✅ - Default 0 ms. Delay of the external vision estimate relative to the IMU. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. Requires reboot. EKF2_EV_NOISE_MD 0 EV-reported variance ✅ - Default 0 (the measurement noise comes from the vision message, with the EV noise parameters as a lower bound; 1 uses the noise parameters directly). Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_POS_X 0.000 m Vision sensor at the CG on X ✅ - Default 0.0. Position of the vision sensor focal point in the body frame. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_POS_Y 0.000 m Vision sensor at the CG on Y ✅ - Default 0.0. Position of the vision sensor focal point in the body frame. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_POS_Z 0.000 m Vision sensor at the CG on Z ✅ - Default 0.0. Position of the vision sensor focal point in the body frame. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_QMIN 0 No minimum vision quality ✅ - Default 0 (range 0 to 100). Minimum quality metric, an optional field some VIO systems provide, for external vision to be started and fused. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EVV_NOISE 0.1 m/s Vision velocity noise 0.1 m/s ✅ - Default 0.1 m/s. Measurement noise for vision velocity measurements, used to lower bound or replace the uncertainty in the message. No motivation to change, and it is not relevant without external vision such as mocap anyway. EKF2_GPS_CHECK 1023 All GPS quality checks enabled ✅ High Default 1023, and it is needed. The 10 bits are satellite count, PDOP, EPH, EPV, speed accuracy, horizontal drift, vertical drift, horizontal speed offset, vertical speed offset, and spoofing. Most tests so far were done with 245 (satellite count, EPH, speed accuracy, horizontal and vertical drift, horizontal speed offset) and without RTK, because Max did not yet know what he was doing. EKF2_GPS_CTRL 7 Lon/lat + altitude + 3D velocity fusion ✅ High Default 7. Dual-antenna heading (bit 3) stays off. EKF2_GPS_DELAY 110 ms GPS delay 110 ms ✅ - Default 110 ms. GPS measurement delay relative to the IMU measurements. No motivation to change. Requires reboot. EKF2_GPS_POS_X 0.010 m GPS antenna 0.010 m forward of CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Measured antenna offset by unknown party. EKF2_GPS_POS_Y 0.000 m GPS antenna on centerline ✅ - Default 0.0. EKF2_GPS_POS_Z −0.217 m GPS antenna 0.217 m above CG (negative Z is up in FRD) ❌ - Default 0.0. Set by Max on 2026-10-27. EKF2_HGT_REF 1 GPS is the height reference ✅ High Default 1. This was contentious. The Astro's GPS vertical fix is much better than the Homebrew's, so without RTK the Homebrew tends to wander vertically when holding position in Position Mode (e.g., 0.5-1 m). Choosing 2 (range sensor) looks like a fix but makes global_position_invalid always true, so transitions into modes such as Hold are declined. This has the consequene that the drone gets stuck taking off (can never transition to Hold from Takeoff) or that it cannot land when using a ROS 2 teleop node if the code first dictates a transition to Hold mode. Hence: use RTK for better estimates and keep 1 so global_position_invalid stays false. (This is the lab's observation; I have not verified the global_position_invalid behaviour in the PX4 source. The source does say the range-sensor option should only be used over a flat surface, because the local NED origin then moves with ground level.) EKF2_IMU_POS_X 0.0587 m IMU 0.0587 m forward of CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Max does not know who set this or where the value came from. EKF2_IMU_POS_Y 0.000 m IMU on centerline ✅ - Default 0.0. EKF2_IMU_POS_Z −0.051 m IMU 0.051 m above CG (negative Z is up in FRD) ❌ - Default 0.0. Set by Max on 2026-10-27. EKF2_MAG_CHECK 1 Magnetic field strength check only ✅ - Default 1 (strength only). Bitmask of the checks that decide whether the magnetometer data is valid: bit 0 field strength (tolerance EKF2_MAG_CHK_STR, 0.2 gauss), bit 1 field inclination (EKF2_MAG_CHK_INC, 20 degrees), bit 2 wait for GNSS to provide the theoretical strength and inclination from the World Magnetic Model (WMM). If GNSS data is received the field is compared with the WMM, otherwise with an average value. The check is useful to reject occasional hard-iron disturbances, and with COM_ARM_MAG_STR = 1 a failed check denies arming. Max would enable all the checks (7), but everything works and he has never broken a magnetometer in a crash, so there is no motivation to move away from the default. EKF2_MIN_RNG 0.01 m Expected ground range 0.01 m ❌ - Default 0.1 m. The range finder reading the estimator assumes when the vehicle is on the ground and not moving, and the range finder returns invalid data or none, for example because it is inside its minimum measurement distance. The terrain estimator then still has a terrain height at the start of flight. Max applies 0.01 m (the lowest allowed value) early, because it is expected to become the default in PX4 1.18 (not verified by me). EKF2_MULTI_IMU 3 Run 3 EKFs, one per IMU ❌ - Default 0 (disabled). The flight controller has 3 IMUs inside, and letting PX4 pick the best estimate among them is a good idea. Requires SENS_IMU_MODE = 0. Requires reboot. PX4 only rewrites this value itself when it is outside 1 to 4 while SENS_IMU_MODE is 0. EKF2_MULTI_MAG 0 Multi-EKF magnetometers disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). Maximum number of magnetometers to use for Multi-EKF; it requires SENS_MAG_MODE = 0 and a reboot. Left disabled because, unlike the IMUs, Max reports that the Cube does not have multiple magnetometers. The Here4 also provides a compass over DroneCAN (UAVCAN_SUB_MAG), so PX4 sees more than one. As far as I can tell, the sensors module chooses between them by priority and health (see the CAL_MAGn_PRIO parameters), not through UAVCAN_ENABLE. Max thinks both are reasonably accurate but is not sure which one is in use. If magnetometer issues appear, this is a good place to start. EKF2_OF_CTRL 1 Optical flow fusion enabled ✅ - Default is 1 in v1.16. Kept explicit so flow is always used. Flow data arrives over CAN (see UAVCAN_SUB_FLOW). EKF2_OF_POS_X 0.04440 m Flow sensor 0.0444 m forward of CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_OF_POS_Y 0.06670 m Flow sensor 0.0667 m right of CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_OF_POS_Z 0.05080 m Flow sensor 0.0508 m below CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_REQ_EPH 3.0 m Maximum 3.0 m horizontal position error to use GPS ✅ - Default 3.0 m (range 2 to 100). Maximum horizontal position error (EPH) the GPS may report for it to be used (bit 2 of EKF2_GPS_CHECK). Active because EKF2_GPS_CHECK = 1023. This threshold does not require RTK by itself, so the offboard code should land immediately, or refuse to arm, whenever the GPS fix type is not 6 (RTK fixed). EKF2_REQ_EPV 5.0 m Maximum 5.0 m vertical position error to use GPS ✅ - Default 5.0 m (range 2 to 100). Maximum vertical position error (EPV) the GPS may report for it to be used (bit 3 of EKF2_GPS_CHECK). Active because EKF2_GPS_CHECK = 1023. This threshold does not require RTK by itself, so the offboard code should land immediately, or refuse to arm, whenever the GPS fix type is not 6 (RTK fixed). EKF2_REQ_HDRIFT 0.1 m/s Maximum 0.1 m/s horizontal drift to use GPS ✅ - Default 0.1 m/s (range 0.1 to 1.0, so this is also the strictest allowed value). Maximum horizontal drift speed, used for the horizontal position drift and horizontal speed offset checks (bits 5 and 7 of EKF2_GPS_CHECK). The drift and offset checks only run when the vehicle is on the ground and stationary. Active because EKF2_GPS_CHECK = 1023. This threshold does not require RTK by itself, so the offboard code should land immediately, or refuse to arm, whenever the GPS fix type is not 6 (RTK fixed). EKF2_REQ_NSATS 6 At least 6 satellites to use GPS ✅ - Default 6 (range 4 to 12). Minimum satellite count for the GPS to be used (bit 0 of EKF2_GPS_CHECK). Active because EKF2_GPS_CHECK = 1023. This threshold does not require RTK by itself, so the offboard code should land immediately, or refuse to arm, whenever the GPS fix type is not 6 (RTK fixed). EKF2_REQ_PDOP 2.5 Maximum PDOP 2.5 to use GPS ✅ - Default 2.5 (range 1.5 to 5.0). Maximum position dilution of precision for the GPS to be used (bit 1 of EKF2_GPS_CHECK). Active because EKF2_GPS_CHECK = 1023. This threshold does not require RTK by itself, so the offboard code should land immediately, or refuse to arm, whenever the GPS fix type is not 6 (RTK fixed). EKF2_REQ_SACC 0.5 m/s Maximum 0.5 m/s speed accuracy to use GPS ✅ - Default 0.5 m/s (range 0.5 to 5.0, so this is also the strictest allowed value). Maximum speed accuracy the GPS may report for it to be used (bit 4 of EKF2_GPS_CHECK). No motivation to change. EKF2_REQ_VDRIFT 0.2 m/s Maximum 0.2 m/s vertical drift to use GPS ✅ - Default 0.2 m/s (range 0.1 to 1.5). Maximum vertical drift speed, used for the vertical position drift and vertical speed offset checks (bits 6 and 8 of EKF2_GPS_CHECK). Like the horizontal ones, these only run when the vehicle is on the ground and stationary. No motivation to change. EKF2_RNG_A_HMAX 5.0 m Range aid up to 5.0 m height ✅ - Default 5.0 m (range 1 to 10). Maximum height above ground for the conditional range aid (EKF2_RNG_CTRL = 1): above it the estimator stops fusing the range finder for height. EKF2_RNG_A_VMAX 1.0 m/s Range aid up to 1.0 m/s horizontal speed ✅ - Default 1.0 m/s (range 0.1 to 2). Maximum horizontal speed for the conditional range aid (EKF2_RNG_CTRL = 1): above it the estimator stops fusing the range finder for height. EKF2_RNG_CTRL 1 Range finder enabled (conditional mode) ✅ High Default 1. Range aiding is used at low speed and low altitude (takeoff/landing). EKF2_RNG_POS_X −0.00635 m Rangefinder 0.00635 m behind CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_RNG_POS_Y 0.0539 m Rangefinder 0.0539 m right of CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_RNG_POS_Z 0.114 m Rangefinder 0.114 m below CG ❌ - Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset.

docs.title: FD: Failure Detector
docs.text:
All FD_ACT_* parameters stay at their defaults, and the check is on by default. If the motors do not draw the small amount of current expected for the commanded throttle, PX4 treats that as a motor failure and warns accordingly (the reaction is set by COM_ACT_FAIL_ACT, which is warning only here). The check works from ESC current, so it can only trigger if the ESCs report current telemetry; the notes for COM_ARM_CHK_ESCS say these ESCs do not, which would make this check inert on this vehicle (my inference; not verified in the source).

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason FD_ACT_EN 1 Actuator failure check enabled ✅ - Default 1 (enabled). The failure detector verifies that each motor consumes a minimum amount of ESC current per throttle level; otherwise it indicates a motor failure. Leave at default. Requires reboot. FD_ACT_MOT_C2T 2.0 A/% Current-to-throttle threshold 2.0 A/% ✅ - Default 2.0 (range 0 to 50). A motor failure triggers only below this ESC current per throttle value. Leave at default. FD_ACT_MOT_THR 0.2 Motor failure only above 20 % throttle ✅ - Default 0.2 (normalized 0 to 1, not percent). A motor failure is only evaluated above this throttle value. Leave at default. FD_ACT_MOT_TOUT 100 ms Violation must last 100 ms ✅ - Default 100 ms (range 10 to 10000). The throttle threshold and the current-to-throttle threshold must both be violated for this long before a motor failure triggers. Leave at default.

docs.title: GF: Geofence
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason GF_ACTION 5 Land mode on geofence violation ❌ - Default 2 (Hold mode). Land immediately rather than hover. GF_MAX_VER_DIST 0 m Disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). Do not use this feature. Because the GPS fix moves during the 1-10 minute initial RTK fix, the relative altitude (relative to the fix when it first boots) will make the quadcopter think it's all over the place. Since you cannot reset the home position without arming, using this feature to prevent the quadcopter from hitting the net as an extra safety feature is moot. Just use CBFs. This feature would interfere with CBF offboard code anyways. If not using RTK (you should really just use it), the estimates are likely not good enough to prevent you from hitting the net. And, PX4's geofence does not take into account for instance the speed at which you approach a geofence, so it's not even enforceable as a never-cross-this boundary.

docs.title: GPS: Serial GPS
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason GPS_1_CONFIG 0 Serial GPS driver disabled ❌ - Default 201 (GPS 1). The GPS is the Here4 on DroneCAN, so the serial GPS driver stays off.

docs.title: MAN: Manual Control
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason MAN_ARM_GESTURE 0 Stick arm/disarm gesture disabled ❌ - Default 1 (enabled). Prevents accidental arming/disarming by stick position. MAN_KILL_GEST_T −1 Kill stick gesture disabled ✅ - Default −1 (negative value disables the feature).

docs.title: MAV: MAVLink
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason MAV_0_CONFIG 101 MAVLink instance 0 on TELEM 1 ✅ - Default 101 (TELEM 1). The QGC telemetry radio connects here. Requires reboot. If torque-level control is ever wanted, note that (per Max, not verified by me) MAVROS does not support torque-level commands but uXRCE-DDS does, while RTK is not possible over uXRCE-DDS because there is no topic for it yet. Torque-level control plus RTK would therefore need uXRCE-DDS and MAVROS running together. That would need a third serial port, because TELEM 1 and TELEM 2 are taken by the QGC radio and the Jetson link, and giving up the QGC radio is extremely dangerous for a torque-level offboard flight. Options are to wait until uXRCE-DDS supports RTK or MAVROS supports torque-level control, to write custom PX4 topics for RTK over uXRCE-DDS, or to solder a new cable and run uXRCE-DDS on another port such as GPS 2 (not tried). MAV_1_CONFIG 102 MAVLink instance 1 on TELEM 2 ❌ High Default 0 (disabled). The FTDI-to-USB cable to the Jetson connects to the flight controller here. Requires reboot. MAV_1_FLOW_CTRL 2 Serial flow control auto-detected ✅ - Default 2. The Jetson link. This setting tells PX4 to auto-detect flow control; PX4 does not write the parameter itself. Use 0 or 1 only if auto-detection fails. Requires reboot. MAV_1_FORWARD 0 No message forwarding from the Jetson link ✅ - Default 0. Broadcast messages (or ones aimed at another system) arriving on the Jetson link are not forwarded to the other MAVLink links. Requires reboot. MAV_1_MODE 2 Onboard message set ✅ - Default 2 (Onboard). The set of streamed messages on the Jetson link is the one meant for a companion computer. Requires reboot. MAV_1_RATE 0 B/s Rate limit chosen from the baud rate ✅ - Default 0. With 0, PX4 uses half the theoretical bandwidth, baud/20 bytes per second; at 921600 baud that is 46080 B/s. PX4 does not write the parameter itself. Requires reboot. MAV_PROTO_VER 2 Always use MAVLink 2 ❌ - Default 0 (start with MAVLink 1 and switch to 2 if the GCS sends version 2). Forces MAVLink 2.0 instead of 1.0. Not super critical; revert to the default if there are problems. MAV_SYS_ID TBD (2–249) Unique number per homebrew vehicle ❌ High Default 1. Never use 1 (every Astro requires 1 and it can't be changed). Choosing 1 will cause ROS 2 topic to intermingle between the Astro and Homebrew despite being namespaced. Must be unique. Range 1–250; never pick 250. Requires reboot. MAV_TYPE 2 Quadrotor ✅ - MC default 2 (metadata 0, generic micro air vehicle, overridden by rc.mc_defaults). The airframe type announced over MAVLink. Not super critical.

docs.title: MC: Multicopter Autotune
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason MC_AIRMODE 0 Air-mode disabled ✅ High Default 0 (disabled). Air-mode changes which commands are prioritized when the controller is saturating. Disabled is what Max recommends and has tested with. MC_AT_EN 1 Autotune module enabled ❌ - Default 0 (disabled). Allows autotuning the control cascade from QGC. This does not mean the quad tunes continuously in flight. Do not run it unless there is a reason to suspect poor control performance, which there really should not be. MC_BAT_SCALE_EN 1 Battery power level scaler enabled ❌ High Default 0 (disabled). This compensates for the voltage drop of the battery over time by attempting to normalize performance. It is important so that experiments run on a low battery perform similarly to a nearly full battery.

docs.title: MIS: Mission
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT 2.5 m Take off to 2.5 m from ground level ✅ - Default 2.5 m. Take off to 2.5 m from ground level

docs.title: MPC: Multicopter Position Control
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason MPC_LAND_RC_HELP 0 Stick nudging during Land disabled ✅ - Default 0. Deliberately left at default. Enabling it lets the sticks move the quad horizontally and yaw it during PX4's Land and Descend modes, and scales the descent speed with the throttle stick (full up stops the descent, centered is MPC_LAND_SPEED, full down is double). The trade-off and collisions: (1) the v1.16 description says stick override of auto modes must be disabled for this to work, which collides with COM_RC_OVERRIDE = 3; with override on, a fast stick movement in an auto mode switches to Position mode instead of nudging, and COM_RC_STICK_OV sets how sensitive that is. Max prefers the override. (2) The throttle stick on a Taranis QX7 does not spring back to center, so an RC left on with throttle low would double the descent speed of every Land, including a battery failsafe Land (COM_LOW_BAT_ACT) (my inference from the description). (3) It has no effect in Offboard, so it does not change Jetson landings, and it needs a valid RC, so it does nothing on a quad with no RC. (4) MPC_LAND_RADIUS (default 1000 m) limits how far the nudging can move the quad from the landing point. MPC_THR_HOVER 0.55 Hover thrust 0.55 ❌ High Default 0.5. Works well. Increase it if adding a payload. Do not exceed 0.7.

docs.title: NAV: Navigator
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason NAV_DLL_ACT 0 Disabled (no GCS-loss failsafe) ✅ High Default 0. Removes the need for QGC to stay connected. Required for multi-agent setups. NAV_RCL_ACT 3 Land mode on RC loss ❌ High Default 2 (Return mode). Land in place instead of returning.

docs.title: PLD: Precision Landing
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason PLD_SRCH_ALT 2.5 m Climb to 2.5 m above home when searching for the landing target ❌ - Default 10 m. Our flight space has a net at 8 m.

These are what the motors for this quadcopter need. Output functions 101 to 104 are Motor 1 to Motor 4.

PWM_MAIN_FUNC2 102 Motor 2 ❌ - Default 0 (disabled). What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_FUNC3 103 Motor 3 ❌ - Default 0 (disabled). What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_FUNC4 104 Motor 4 ❌ - Default 0 (disabled). What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_MAX1 1900 Output 1 maximum 1900 µs ❌ - Default 2000. What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_MAX2 1900 Output 2 maximum 1900 µs ❌ - Default 2000. What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_MAX3 1900 Output 3 maximum 1900 µs ❌ - Default 2000. What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_MAX4 1900 Output 4 maximum 1900 µs ❌ - Default 2000. What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_MIN1 1100 Output 1 minimum 1100 µs ❌ - Default 1000. What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_MIN2 1100 Output 2 minimum 1100 µs ❌ - Default 1000. What the motors for this quadcopter need. PWM_MAIN_MIN3 1100 Output 3 minimum 1100 µs ❌ - Default 1000. What the motors for this quadcopter need.
