docs.title: RC: Radio Control
docs.text:
These are the Taranis QX7 template needed to use the radio with this quadcopter.

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason RC_CHAN_CNT 18 18 RC channels saved at RC calibration ❌ - Default 0. Taranis QX7 template needed to use this radio with the quadcopter. RC_KILLSWITCH_TH 0.75 Kill switch threshold 0.75 ✅ - Default 0.75. Fine as is. RC_MAP_ARM_SW 9 Arm switch on RC channel 9 ❌ - Default 0 (unassigned). Taranis QX7 template needed to use this radio with the quadcopter. RC_MAP_AUX1 0 AUX1 unassigned ✅ - Default 0 (unassigned). Channel 10 is the kill switch (RC_MAP_KILL_SW), so AUX1 must not also use it. RC_MAP_FLTMODE 5 Flight mode selection on RC channel 5 ❌ - Default 0 (unassigned). Taranis QX7 template needed to use this radio with the quadcopter. RC_MAP_KILL_SW 10 Kill switch on RC channel 10 ❌ - Default 0 (unassigned). Channel 10 is the right switch on the Taranis QX7. RC_MAP_PITCH 2 Pitch on RC channel 2 ❌ - Default 0 (unassigned). Taranis QX7 template needed to use this radio with the quadcopter. RC_MAP_ROLL 1 Roll on RC channel 1 ❌ - Default 0 (unassigned). Taranis QX7 template needed to use this radio with the quadcopter. RC_MAP_THROTTLE 3 Throttle on RC channel 3 ❌ - Default 0 (unassigned). Taranis QX7 template needed to use this radio with the quadcopter. RC_MAP_YAW 4 Yaw on RC channel 4 ❌ - Default 0 (unassigned). Taranis QX7 template needed to use this radio with the quadcopter.

docs.title: RTL: Return Mode
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason RTL_DESCEND_ALT 2 m 2 m (≈ 6.6 ft) ❌ - MC default 10 m (metadata 30 m, overridden by rc.mc_defaults). The net is 8 m tall, so this keeps the vehicle clear of it. RTL_RETURN_ALT 2 m 2 m (≈ 6.6 ft) ❌ - MC default 30 m (metadata 60 m, overridden by rc.mc_defaults). The net is 8 m tall, so this keeps the vehicle clear of it.

docs.title: SDLOG: SD Logging
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason SDLOG_PROFILE 1 Default logging set only ✅ High Default 1. Our SD cards have a limited maximum write rate (5 MB/s). More logging helps advanced debugging, but the SD cards we have now cannot keep up with more writes than SDLOG_PROFILE = 1. See Known Issues. Requires reboot.

docs.title: SENS: Sensors
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason SENS_BOARD_ROT 2 Autopilot board rotated Yaw 90° ❌ - Default 0 (no rotation). Required for how the CubePilot is placed in the case. This setting tells PX4 the arrow on the CubePilot points to the drone's starboard (clockwise is positive). Requires reboot. SENS_EN_PMW3901 0 Local PMW3901 optical flow driver disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). This enables a PMW3901 wired to the Cube's SPI bus. The optical flow sensor is on CAN instead (see UAVCAN_SUB_FLOW). SENS_EN_SF0X 8 LW20/c ❌ - Default 1 (SF02). Selects the model of the serial LightWare lidar. It only appears when SENS_SF0X_CFG is not disabled, so it does not need to be set (and is not in the .params file). SENS_EN_SF1XX 6 SF/LW20/c ❌ - Default 0 (disabled). The LW20/c on I2C is the only distance sensor used for estimation. Requires reboot. SENS_FLOW_ROT 0 No rotation ✅ - Default 0 (no rotation). Rotation of the optical flow sensor relative to the airframe. It seems to work fine at 0, but Max was not able to verify which direction the optical flow sensor faces. SENS_IMU_MODE 0 Sensors hub does not select the primary IMU (needed for multi-EKF) ❌ - Default 1 (publish primary IMU selection). Required by EKF2_MULTI_IMU = 3: the v1.16 description of EKF2_MULTI_IMU says "Requires SENS_IMU_MODE 0". Requires reboot. SENS_SF0X_CFG 0 Disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). Serial port configuration for the LightWare lidar (that is, UART). Since the LW20/c is on I2C (SENS_EN_SF1XX), this stays disabled to prevent PX4 from getting confused.

docs.title: SEP: Septentrio GPS
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason SEP_PORT1_CFG 0 Septentrio driver disabled ✅ - Default 0 (disabled). The GPS is the Here4 on DroneCAN, so the Septentrio serial driver stays off.

docs.title: SER: Serial Ports
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason SER_TEL1_BAUD 57600 TELEM 1 at 57600 baud ✅ - Default 57600. The QGC telemetry radio on TELEM 1 (MAV_0_CONFIG); the radio must use the same baud rate. Requires reboot. SER_TEL2_BAUD 921600 TELEM 2 at 921600 baud ✅ - Default 921600. The Jetson link on TELEM 2 (MAV_1_CONFIG). Requires reboot.

docs.title: SF1XX: LightWare Lidar (I2C)
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason SF1XX_MODE 1 Enabled ✅ - Default 1 (enabled). Operation mode of the LightWare lidar driver. The other option, 2 (disabled during VTOL fast forward flight), is for VTOL vehicles and is not relevant here.

docs.title: SYS: System
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason SYS_AUTOSTART 4001 Generic Quadcopter (airframe 4001_quad_x) ❌ - Default 0 (none). Uses the multicopter for PX4 default parameters. Requires reboot. SYS_HAS_BARO 1 Barometer expected ✅ - Default 1 (on). Pre-flight check for a barometer; if disabled, the preflight checks do not look for one. Requires reboot. SYS_HAS_GPS 1 GPS expected ✅ - Default 1 (on). Controls whether the vehicle has a GPS. If disabled, the sensors hub does not process sensor_gps at all and GPS is not available to the rest of the system, so this must stay on. Requires reboot. SYS_HAS_MAG 1 One magnetometer expected ✅ - Default 1 (on). Number of magnetometers the pre-flight check requires: 0 means none is expected, and 1 to N require N magnetometers to be present. Requires reboot. SYS_HAS_NUM_DIST 1 One distance sensor required ❌ High Default 0 (check disabled). The preflight check fails if fewer than this number of distance sensors with valid data are present. Set to 1 so that a missing or silent LW20/c is caught before flight. SYS_HAS_NUM_OF 1 One optical flow sensor required ❌ High Default 0 (check disabled). The preflight check fails if fewer than this number of optical flow sensors with valid data are present (the maximum is 1). Set to 1 so that a missing or silent flow sensor is caught before flight. SYS_USB_AUTO 2 MAVLink starts on USB right away ✅ - Default 2 (MAVLink). Per the PX4 serial configuration documentation, it selects whether the USB port runs no particular protocol, auto-detects the protocol, or is set to MAVLink. With MAVLink, PX4 starts MAVLink on USB as soon as USB is available instead of waiting to receive data first. Keep it at default so the USB link works right away.

docs.title: THR: Thrust Model
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason THR_MDL_FAC 0.3 Thrust model factor 0.3 (30% quadratic term) ❌ High Default 0. Usually determined by a bench thrust test. This value is a good guess that works in flight, so there is no motivation to change it.

docs.title: UAVCAN: DroneCAN
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason UAVCAN_ENABLE 2 Sensors, automatic config ❌ - Default 0 (disabled). DroneCAN must be on for the Here4 and the flow/rangefinder node. Value 2 allocates node IDs dynamically. Requires reboot. UAVCAN_PUB_RTCM 1 Publish RTCM stream ❌ - Default 0. Required for PX4 to accept RTK corrections over DroneCAN. Requires reboot. UAVCAN_RNG_MAX 100 m Rangefinder maximum range 100 m ❌ - Default 999 m. The maximum valid range accepted from a rangefinder connected over DroneCAN. 100 m is the rated maximum range of the LW20/c. As far as I can tell from the description, it only applies to a DroneCAN rangefinder (UAVCAN_SUB_RNG, which is 0 here) and not to the LW20/c on I2C. UAVCAN_RNG_MIN 0 m Rangefinder minimum range 0 m ✅ - Default 0 m. The minimum valid range accepted from a rangefinder connected over DroneCAN. Technically the rated minimum for the LW20/c is 0.2 m, but this works so it is fine. The same caveat as for UAVCAN_RNG_MAX applies. UAVCAN_SUB_FLOW 1 Optical flow subscription enabled ❌ High Default 0. The optical flow sensor is on the CAN bus. This subscribes to its flow data only; its distance sensor is controlled separately by UAVCAN_SUB_RNG. Requires reboot. UAVCAN_SUB_GPS 1 GPS subscription enabled ✅ - Default 1. The Here4 provides GPS over DroneCAN. Requires reboot. UAVCAN_SUB_IMU 0 IMU subscription disabled ✅ - Default 0. No external IMU on CAN; the IMUs are inside the Cube. Requires reboot. UAVCAN_SUB_MAG 1 Magnetometer subscription enabled ✅ - Default 1. The Here4 provides a compass over DroneCAN. Max is not sure this compass is actually the one being used (see EKF2_MULTI_MAG). Requires reboot. UAVCAN_SUB_RNG 0 Range finder subscription disabled ✅ - Default 0. The only distance sensor is the LW20/c on I2C. The optical flow sensor's own distance sensor must never be used for estimation. Requires reboot.

docs.title: USB: USB MAVLink
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason USB_MAV_MODE 2 Onboard message set on USB ✅ - Default 2 (Onboard). The MAVLink profile used on the USB port when MAVLink is set or detected (SYS_USB_AUTO). The PX4 documentation says the USB port is by default a MAVLink port with the onboard profile meant for companion computers, the same message set as MAV_1_MODE.

docs.title: uXRCE: A MAVROS Alternative
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Relevance Reason UXRCE_DDS_CFG 0 Disabled ✅ - Default 0. Turns on the UXRCE-DDS Client (alternative to MAVROS that allows torque-level control but foregoes RTK). UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID 0 ROS Domain ID ✅ - Default 0. Must match ROS setup. UXRCE_DDS_PTCFG 2 Custom participant ❌ - Default 0. Required if using discovery server. Needs a XML config and file on fs/microsd/etc/. This parameter only appears if UXRCE_DDS_CFG is not zero. Ignore if not using uXCRE.

docs.title: PX4 Configuration
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-10-21Autonomy Park

At a glance

Every Homebrew quadcopter is configured the same way and then calibrated on its own. Skipping a step, or reusing another drone's calibration, causes intermittent problems and crashes.

Written for QGC 5.1.5

This guide was written for QGroundControl (QGC) 5.1.5. The QGC interface was reworked in 5.1.x, so the menus in 5.0.x look different and the menu paths in this guide will not match. If you use 5.0.x, expect to hunt for the equivalent menu.

QGC 5.1.x and Later Has No Ubuntu 22.04 Binary

QGC 5.1.x and later do not provide binaries for Ubuntu 22.04. On Ubuntu 22.04 you must build QGC from scratch. QGC 5.0.8 is fine to use for the foreseeable future.

Read Parameters in the PX4 v1.16 Reference Only

To understand any parameter in this guide, Homebrew Parameters, or Calibration Parameters, use the PX4 v1.16 parameter reference. Do not use the main (latest) reference: parameters differ between PX4 versions.

These Parameters Configure MAVROS, Not uXRCE-DDS

The parameter template below configures MAVROS (tested with MAVROS 2.16.0). It does not configure the Micro XRCE-DDS Agent. Torque-level offboard commands need the Micro XRCE-DDS Agent, because MAVROS does not support them.

As of PX4 1.17.0 (and so 1.16.2), the Micro XRCE-DDS Agent exposes no topic for serving RTK corrections to PX4. With MAVROS, an NTRIP client on a companion computer publishes the corrections to <mavros_namespace>/mavros/gps_rtk/send_rtcm.

Pull request #29368 (RTK corrections over uXRCE-DDS) is not part of any stable PX4 release. To experiment with torque-level control together with RTK, you must build mainline PX4 and port every parameter to the current PX4 parameter reference.

RTK Corrections Are Not Served Through QGC

As of QGC 5.1.5, serving RTK corrections through QGC does not work, even though it is advertised as a feature. The QGC developers admit that no one has field-tested it, and Max's field test failed. The Autonomy Park serves RTK corrections to the robots a different way, and nobody should serve RTK through QGC anyway: it is extra setup for no reason.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• QGroundControl (QGC), see the notes above for the version. Install details: Software We Use.
  • A USB connection to the flight controller, directly or through the spare dongle (see Wired (USB)).
  • A wireless telemetry radio for the calibrations (see Wireless (Radio)).
  • A LiPo voltage checker for the battery voltage calibration (see "Battery Voltage Calibration" in Sensor Calibration).
  • The files in the Files section.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Use these direct links for configuration and recovery. Do not use older versions unless specifically troubleshooting legacy hardware.

File Type Description Link Firmware Binary Stable PX4 v1.16.2 for the CubePilot Cube Orange cubepilot_cubeorange_default_1_16_2.px4 Parameter Template Parameters for the Homebrew airframes on PX4 1.16.2. It contains no calibration values, so it is safe to load again and again on any quadcopter homebrew-px4-v1.16.2.params Parameter Reference What each parameter in the template is set to, and why Homebrew Parameters Calibration Parameters The per-drone parameters that are never copied between quadcopters Calibration and Per-Drone Parameters Comparison Script Python script that compares two or more parameter files and lists the differences, leaving out the calibration parameters px4-param-diff.py

The parameter template is applied on top of the default multicopter parameters for PX4 1.16.2. The Clean Configuration Procedure gives the full procedure.

To compare parameter files, run this on your computer in the folder that holds the script and the files:

uv run px4-param-diff.py --files <first.params> <second.params> --output_csv <differences.csv>

docs.title: Upgrading Firmware
docs.text: Upgrading PX4 is covered on its own page: Upgrading PX4 Firmware.

docs.title: Wired (USB)
docs.text:
Use for flashing firmware, configuring the Actuators tab, and high-speed data transfer.

  • Safety: Start with the drone disconnected from the battery and all propellers removed. Connect to the computer via USB (directly to the Flight Controller or the spare dongle).

docs.title: Wireless (Radio)
docs.text:
Use for sensor calibration and general telemetry.

  • Baud Rate: Ensure the baud rate is set to 57600. If QGC shows a default, leave it at this value.
  • Limitation: The Actuators tab is inaccessible via radio; it will revert to the legacy Motors tab. Do not modify settings here.
  • QGC setup of the radio: Not yet documented.
  • Linux Permission: If opening the port fails because of dialout permissions, add your user to the dialout group, then restart the machine.

On Linux, add your user to the dialout group:

sudo usermod -a -G dialout $USER

docs.title: Manual Connection Discovery
docs.text:
If autoconnect fails, identify the port and set permissions.

Linux / WSLmacOSWindows

List the serial devices:

ls /dev/tty*

Not verified on WSL.

List the serial devices. You may see something like /dev/cu.usbserial-B0048D22:

ls /dev/cu.*

Give yourself permission to use the port you found. Skipping this results in a "Permission error when locking device" message:

sudo chmod 666 /dev/cu.<id>

In PowerShell, list the USB devices to identify the COM port:

Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly | Where-Object { $_.InstanceId -match 'USB' }

Use the COM port it reports.

Not verified on Windows.

docs.title: Clean Configuration Procedure
docs.text:
Perform these steps via USB. Start with no propellers and no battery connected, and add the battery only when a step tells you to. Note that not all aspects are stored as parameters (e.g., Airframe type and ESC Calibration), which is why some things can come before loading the set of Parameters.

  1. Firmware Flash: In the Firmware tab, follow the instructions to flash custom firmware, selecting cubepilot_cubeorange_default_1_16_2.px4.

  2. Reset: In the Parameters tab, open the Tools menu and select Reset all to firmware's defaults.

    Never Reset to Vehicle Defaults

    Never use Reset to vehicle's configuration defaults for this step. Use Reset all to firmware's defaults.

  3. Reboot: Use the Reboot Vehicle button in QGC (Q icon > Configure > Parameters > Tools > Reboot Vehicle).

  4. Airframe: Select Generic Quadcopter (Quad X). Ignore the red sensor errors in the log for now.

    What This Step Does

    Selecting Generic Quadcopter (Quad X) is the same as setting SYS_AUTOSTART to 4001 and SYS_AUTOCONFIG to 1 in the Parameters tab and then rebooting. It applies a series of defaults that every quadcopter needs. These defaults are the base that the parameter template in step 7 is applied on top of.

    PX4 handles many more vehicle types than quadcopters. The template does not necessarily apply to any of them.

  5. Reboot: Again.

  6. ESC Calibration: Follow the QGC wizard. Ensure propellers are removed before plugging in the battery when prompted.

    Done Once, Ever

    ESC calibration must be done once, ever, unless the ESCs are changed. It is one of the few things that is not stored in PX4.

    PX4's v1.16 documentation says this calibration is only for PWM and OneShot ESCs: DShot and CAN ESCs do not need it. The Homebrews are configured for PWM.

  7. Template: Load the PX4 template for the Homebrews: homebrew-px4-v1.16.2.params.

  8. Reboot: Final reboot to commit parameter changes.

  9. Sensor Calibration: The template contains no calibration values, so every calibration in Sensor Calibration must be done, including the battery voltage calibration.

Load the Template Before You Calibrate

The template sets parameters that the calibrations rely on, such as SENS_BOARD_ROT. Never calibrate first and load the template afterward, even though the template contains no per-drone calibration values.

docs.title: Sensor Calibration
docs.text:
Never Calibrate Sensors Over USB

Compass calibration requires continuous slow spinning. A USB cable will snag, tangle, and can damage the flight controller port or the cable itself. Use the wireless radio.

Disconnect USB and switch to the wireless radio. Seal the drone up for a firm grip.

Do all four sensor calibrations: Level Horizon, Gyroscope, Accelerometer, and Compass. Then do the battery voltage calibration below.

The recommended order is Level Horizon, Gyroscope, Accelerometer, then Compass. The order is recommended, not required. The first two can be done by setting the quadcopter on the ground, without rebooting it.

Never Reuse Another Drone's Calibration Values

Calibration values are unique to each quadcopter. Reusing them causes intermittent problems and crashes. Every drone has its own magnetic interference (soft and hard iron) and IMU biases, so another drone's calibration makes measurements drift or triggers EKF failures. PX4 will never throw an error because as far as it knows, sensors have non-default calibration values which implies a correct set of calibrations. The Homebrew parameter template contains no calibration values, but a parameter file exported from another drone does. Always calibrate each drone individually.

docs.title: Battery Voltage Calibration
docs.text:
Calibrate battery voltage using a physical voltmeter for reference: the LiPo voltage checker shown below. The battery sensing values are unique to each quadcopter (see Calibration Parameters).

Example of a physical voltmeter: a LiPo voltage checker.

docs.title: Firmware Management
docs.text:
To flash PX4 you need a .px4 file for the platform you want. For us that is the CubePilot Orange. We also have CubePilot Blue controllers, which are functionally identical, so they use the same file. This is not the file for the CubePilot Orange+.

When you flash from QGC's Firmware tab, QGC downloads the latest stable PX4 automatically. Getting an older version, or a newer one before it is stable, requires building it: see Building PX4.

We keep the .px4 file here for simplicity: cubepilot_cubeorange_default_1_16_2.px4. Back up the .px4 file of any future PX4 version you use.

docs.title: Parameters vs. Calibrations
docs.text: Not everything is stored in a .params file. Sensor calibrations are stored as parameters, but they are unique to each quadcopter and are never copied between drones (see Sensor Calibration). ESC calibration is not stored in PX4 at all (see step 6 in section 4.0).

docs.title: RTK Setup
docs.text:
Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

A Homebrew gets RTK corrections automatically once the ground station is on, homebrew_docker is set up, and the parameters are set.

RTK corrections make GPS position centimeter-level accurate, allowing much better precisse handling and repeatability of experiments. We require RTK to guarantee that altitude estimation is accurate enough to prevent collisions with the net. A ground station at a known position sends corrections to the robot, which uses them to remove the GPS error it shares with the ground station.

Start the Homebrew Outdoors

Start the Homebrew outdoors, never indoors.

Follow these in order. After them, RTK works.

  1. Watch the Homebrew setup video.
  2. Follow the instructions in homebrew_docker. It contains the NTRIP client that takes corrections from the RTKLib caster. Use the RTKLib caster, never the RS3's embedded caster.
  3. Follow RTK Setup so the ground station is on.
  4. Check that the parameters are set as described in PX4 Configuration.

To see whether each Homebrew has homebrew_docker set up, see the table Status of Each Homebrew.

docs.title: Arm-Motor Subassembly Instructions
docs.text:
Written by Mingyuan (Damian) GaoUpdated 2026-10-21Autonomy Park

At a glance

Assemble one Homebrew arm and motor. This is a step in building a Homebrew.

docs.title: Required Tools
docs.text:
• 2 mm hex screwdriver
  • 2.5 mm hex screwdriver

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Each arm consists of the components shown below.

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text: Remove the 2 mm horizontal screw that goes through the arm tube.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text: Slide in the plastic brackets that will mount the arm to the body plates later.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Place the motor on the motor mount (assemble according to airframe manual) and use four 2.5 mm shoulder screws (same box with the motor) to fasten them. Install all four screws before tightening them.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: Slide the motor mount onto the arm tube with the motor cable facing outward.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Tuck the cables into the arm and push them through to the other end. Place the horizontal screw back in position.

docs.title: ESC Soldering Guide
docs.text:
Written by Mingyuan (Damian) GaoUpdated 2026-10-21Autonomy Park

At a glance

Solder female connectors to an ESC for a Homebrew. The wires are short, so try to get each joint right the first time.

The steps are similar to motor soldering, but we are using female connectors instead.

docs.title: Prepare the ESC and Wires
docs.text:
First, take the ESC out of the box. Be careful to not remove the insulation from the wires unless re-soldering is absolutely necessary.

Handle with Care

The wires are short—try to get it right on the first attempt.

docs.title: Prepare the Connector
docs.text: Grab a female connector and place both it and the wire on a soldering mat, noting that the female connector's end is different from the male version. Align the wire tip inside the connector cup so the insulation meets the end of the connector, then use heavy objects to secure both the wire and the connector in place.

docs.title: Prepare the Soldering Iron
docs.text: To prepare for soldering, turn on the fume extractor or a fan. Set your soldering iron to 400°C (750°F), then clean the tip and tin it by applying a small amount of fresh solder.

docs.title: Solder the Wire to the Connector
docs.text:
Burn Hazard

Avoid touching the hot end of the connector with the iron.

Press the hot iron to the joint where the wire and connector meet. Touch the solder directly to this heated joint—it should melt immediately and flow into the cup. Continue to feed solder into the joint until it fully covers the wire and fills any gaps.

Ensure a Proper Joint

Avoid soldering the outer surface of the connector; the solder should flow into the cup.

docs.title: Check and Secure the Solder Joint
docs.text: Once the joint is filled, remove the iron and allow the solder to cool naturally. If the result is unsatisfactory, you can reheat the joint and add more solder. After it has cooled, use pliers to gently pull the connector to verify it is firmly attached.

docs.title: Apply Heat Shrink Tubing
docs.text: Slide a correctly sized piece of heat shrink tubing over the finished joint, positioning it to completely cover the connector’s circular bulge. Use a heat gun to shrink the tubing until it is snug and secure.

docs.title: Repeat for Remaining Connectors
docs.text: Repeat these steps for the remaining three ESC wires. Once complete, inspect all your solder joints to ensure they are high quality and consistent.

docs.title: Commission the ESC
docs.text: Once all connectors are soldered and secured, the ESC is ready for commissioning.

docs.title: Clean Up
docs.text:
To clean up, turn off the soldering iron, heat gun, and fume extractor. Properly dispose of any leftover wire clippings and other waste materials.

Safety First: Lead Contamination

Although modern solder is often lead-free, it's best practice to treat it as if it contains lead. 🧼 Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water.

docs.title: ESC to PDB Soldering
docs.text:
Written by Mingyuan (Damian) GaoUpdated 2026-10-21Autonomy Park

At a glance

Mount the power distribution board (PDB) and solder the ESC wires to it. This is a step in building a Homebrew.

docs.title: Mounting the Power Distribution Board and Soldering ESC Wires
Mount the PDB
docs.text:
First, clean the contact surfaces on the frame with alcohol. Once dry, place the PDB on the frame using double-sided tape. Make sure the board faces the correct direction as shown in the image; the "front" is marked by the circled tape.

Pro Tip

Use a knife head soldering iron for better surface contact on the pads.

Heat the iron to 850 F for better heat transfer

docs.title: Wire the ESCs
docs.text:
You will use eight pads on the PDB to connect the four ESCs. It is crucial to solder the wires in a counter-clockwise (CCW) order, following the scheme shown in the images below. Depending on the location of the pad, you may need to pre-bend the ESC wire so it reaches without excess slack or tension.

CubePilot Wiring Diagram

docs.title: Follow the Soldering Procedure
docs.text:
Follow these steps carefully to ensure a solid and reliable connection. First, clean the soldering iron tip using brass wool. Apply a tiny bit of flux only if the brass wool doesn't clean it fully.

To tin the pad, touch it with the iron tip and feed in a small amount of solder. Then, tilt the iron to use its slanted surface to spread the solder and completely cover the pad.

Check Soldering Order

If pads are not soldered in a counter-clockwise order, there may not be enough physical space to lay the iron flat and use its slanted side effectively on later pads.

To place the ESC wire, use tweezers to hold the wire tip on the tinned pad. Press the iron tip against the wire until the solder on both the wire and the pad melts together. If they don't melt easily, apply a tiny bit of flux to aid the process.

To reinforce the joint, keep pressing the iron onto the bonded wire and feed in more solder to fully cover it. Be careful to avoid creating solder bridges to adjacent pads or wires.

To cool and check the joint, lift the iron and continue holding the wire with tweezers until the solder is completely cool. A good joint will have a smooth and shiny surface.

Finally, test the connection by gently tugging the wire with tweezers to confirm it is solidly bonded.

Repeat this process for all remaining pads. If a connection fails, clean any flux residue from the pad and try again. It’s completely normal to not get a perfect joint on the first attempt, so take your time.

docs.title: Finish Soldering the PDB
docs.text:
Written by Mingyuan (Damian) GaoUpdated 2026-10-21Autonomy Park

At a glance

Solder the remaining components onto the PDB after the four ESCs. This is a step in building a Homebrew.

Now that we have soldered all four ESCs to the board, there are still a few additional components that need to be soldered.

docs.title: Components to Solder
docs.text:
1. Landing Gear Wire

  2. MAUCH Battery Eliminate Circuit (BEC)

  3. Universal BEC

  4. Battery Connector

docs.title: Solder Pads
docs.text: The picture below shows the pads on the board where these components will be soldered.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text: Components 1 and 3 will be soldered to the same pad. It is recommended to twist the exposed wires together and tape the insulation before soldering, as shown below.

docs.title: Motor Soldering Guide
docs.text:
Written by Mingyuan (Damian) Gao, Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-11-10Autonomy Park

At a glance

Safety, tools, and steps for soldering male connectors to a Homebrew's motor wires. This is a step in building a Homebrew.

Guide for soldering male connectors to motor wires. Read the safety section and gather the tools first.

docs.title: Personal Protective Equipment
docs.text:
• Required: Fume extractor
  • Optional: Mask, gloves, glasses

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Avoid inhaling fumes from burning flux (a polymer).
  • Tie back hair and loose clothing.
  • Always place the soldering iron in its holder when not in use.
  • Do not touch the soldering iron unless unplugged and cooled for at least 5 minutes.
  • Always turn off the soldering iron when walking away.
  • Use pliers to hold workpieces, as they conduct heat quickly.
  • Remove all flammable objects from the workspace.
  • Remove smart watches.
  • Do not use phones at the work station, and wash your hands, to avoid spreading metal or lead traces.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
• Lead-free solder
  • Drone motor
  • 3 male connectors
  • Wire cutters
  • Wire strippers (use the 12-gauge notch)
  • Desoldering wick
  • Work holder (e.g., helping hands)
  • Pliers

docs.title: Prepare the Motor and Wires
docs.text:
• Take the motor out of the box.
  • Use wire cutters to remove the original connectors.

docs.title: Strip the Wire Insulation
docs.text:
• Use a wire stripper to remove about 3mm of insulation.
  • Twist the exposed wire so no strands are loose.

docs.title: Prepare the Connector
docs.text:
• Grab a male connector.
  • Place the wire and connector on a soldering mat.
  • Align the tip of the wire so the insulation meets the connector’s end.

Notice the cone-shaped tip in the image below.

  • Use a heavy object to press down on the wire and another to secure the connector.

docs.title: Prepare the Soldering Iron
docs.text:
• Turn on the fume extractor/fan and your soldering iron.
  • Set the iron to 400°C (750°F).
  • Use the largest soldering tip available, preferably knife-edge. Unscrew and replace the tip carefully, avoiding damage to the heating element.
  • Clean and tin the tip by flicking it in the brass wool and applying solder before use, then place the iron in its holder.

docs.title: Solder the Wire to the Connector
docs.text:
• Press the iron where the wire and connector meet.

Warning

Do not touch the connector’s tip directly — the one below is scrapped.

  • Touch the solder to the iron—it should melt instantly.
  • Feed solder into the joint from the side, until the wire is fully covered and gaps are filled. Feed faster than expected.
  • Aim for a smooth surface finish that contours the connector.

Warning

Avoid soldering the outside surface of the connector.

docs.title: Check and Secure the Solder Joint
docs.text:
• Lift the iron and let the solder cool.
  • If needed, reheat to adjust or add more solder.
  • Once cooled, test the joint’s strength by gently tugging the connector with pliers.

docs.title: Apply Heat Shrink Tubing
docs.text:
• Slide a properly sized heat shrink tube over the connector.
  • Position it to cover the bulge.
  • Use a heat gun to shrink the tubing snugly.

docs.title: Repeat for Remaining Connectors
docs.text:
• Repeat the steps from "Prepare the Motor and Wires" through "Apply Heat Shrink Tubing" for all three motor wires.
  • Inspect all solder joints for consistency and quality.

docs.title: Commission the Motor
docs.text: • Once all connectors are properly soldered and insulated, the motor is ready for use.

docs.title: Clean Up
docs.text:
• Turn off all tools and equipment.
  • Dispose of any leftover material or trash.
  • We use lead-free solder, but treat it like leaded: 🧼 Wash your hands thoroughly.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Dirty soldering tip: Re-tin the tip regularly.
  • Rough surface finish: Use flux and apply heat from the side of the iron, not the tip.
  • Desoldering: Lay the wick on the target area and apply heat from the side of the iron until the solder liquefies.
  • Solder not attaching: Hold the iron on the joint longer to heat all parts (workpiece, wire, and solder) evenly.
  • Excessive errors: Cut the wire, strip, and start over.
  • White surface finish: Caused by excessive heat. Solder faster.
  • Surface imperfections (e.g., black or orange areas): Remelt and add solder, or redo the joint completely.

docs.title: Example Parameters for PX4 Main
docs.text:
Draft. An example for the case study only. Valid only for PX4 main at commit 5f429033bf and the PR 29368 branch on 2026-10-22. Written by Max GardenswartzUpdated 2026-10-22Autonomy Park

At a glance

The parameter reference produced by the porting case study. It is an example of the result, not a template to load on a real Homebrew.

Example Only: Do Not Load These on a Homebrew

These parameters were made for PX4 main at commit 5f429033bf and the open PR #29368 branch, tested on 2026-10-22. Loading them on 1.16.2 or on any stable release can set parameters that do not exist, or that mean something different. The parameters to use on the fleet are in Parameters.

The matching file is example-parameters-px4-main.params. It is also an example only. The method is in Case Study: Porting the Homebrew Parameters to PX4 Main.

Reference: PX4 main at commit 5f429033bf (2026-10-22, the 1.19 development line), with the open pull request #29368 (RTCM corrections over uXRCE-DDS) as the branch under test. This is the main-line port of the v1.16.2 version of this document; the case study shows how it was made. "Default" means the main metadata default plus the CubePilot Cube Orange board defaults (rc.board_defaults), the multicopter defaults in rc.mc_defaults (which overrides RTL_RETURN_ALT and RTL_DESCEND_ALT and sets MAV_TYPE), and the Generic Quadcopter airframe defaults (4001_quad_x, which sets the CA_ROTOR* positions). None of those layered defaults changed from 1.16.2 for the parameters in this document.

Warning

Do not use this for porting to 1.18.0 or any other stable release. Main differs from release/1.18 (for example GNSS_CHECK, GNSS_REQ_* and SENS_GNSS0_* exist only on main; release/1.18 still has EKF2_GPS_CHECK, EKF2_REQ_* and SENS_GPS0_*). Regenerate this document against the target release.

Legend: ✅ = matches the multicopter default, ❌ = differs from the multicopter default.

docs.title: BAT: Battery
docs.text:
Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason BAT1_CAPACITY -1 Disabled ✅ Default −1 (unknown). Left disabled so remaining charge is estimated from voltage only. The current sensor is not working, so coulomb counting would integrate invalid current. Set to 16000 mAh (all Homebrew batteries) once current sensing is verified. BAT1_I_OVERWRITE 0 A Idle-current overwrite disabled ✅ Default 0 (disabled, the measured current is used). BAT1_N_CELLS 6 6S battery ❌ Default 0 (unknown). Should be set by the user to match the battery. BAT1_R_INTERNAL −1 Ω Use the online estimate ✅ Default −1 (use the online estimate). Left at default because the current sensor is not working, and both the sag compensation and the online estimate need valid current. The PX4 parameter description says this is per cell. BAT1_SOURCE 0 Battery 1 read from the power module ✅ Default 0 (labelled "Power Module / Analog" on main, "Power Module" in 1.16.2). The other options are 1 (External, from MAVLink battery status messages) and 2 (ESCs, taken from the esc_status message, which per the v1.16.2 description requires the ESCs to report both voltage and current). PX4 currently cannot read the current from the PDB. Max thinks setting this to 2 might fix that, but this is not verified, and since the notes for COM_ARM_CHK_ESCS say these ESCs do not support telemetry, it may not be possible at all. Requires reboot. BAT1_V_CHARGED 4.2 V 4.2 V per cell when full ✅ Default 4.2 V on main (4.05 V in 1.16.2). The old 4.05 V was a deliberate workaround: the voltage is read from a quadcopter drawing about 5 A, and battery sag makes a full 4.2 V cell read about 4.05 V. Main changed the default and dropped the 1.16.2 description's advice to set this below 4.2 V; Max decided to trust the new default. Remaining charge is a linear interpolation between BAT1_V_EMPTY and BAT1_V_CHARGED (battery.cpp), so at the same measured voltage the estimate is now lower and every threshold below triggers at a higher voltage (more conservative; see BAT_LOW_THR, BAT_CRIT_THR, BAT_EMERGEN_THR, COM_ARM_BAT_MIN). The value also sets the over-voltage "spike" fault threshold (cells × BAT1_V_CHARGED × 1.05) and the battery scale used by MC_BAT_SCALE_EN (default 0, not set here). BAT1_V_EMPTY 3.6 V 3.6 V per cell when empty ✅ Default 3.6 V. The PX4 LiPo default, defined as the per-cell voltage under load when the pack is effectively empty. BAT2_A_PER_V 17 Battery 2 current scale at board default ✅ Default 17 (Cube Orange board default). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_CAPACITY −1 mAh Battery 2 capacity unknown ✅ Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_I_OVERWRITE 0 A Idle-current overwrite disabled ✅ Default 0. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_N_CELLS 0 Cell count unknown ✅ Default 0. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_R_INTERNAL −1 Ω Use the online estimate ✅ Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_SOURCE −1 Battery 2 disabled ✅ Default −1 (Disabled). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_CHANNEL −1 Battery 2 voltage ADC channel at board default ✅ Default −1 (board default). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_CHARGED 4.2 V 4.2 V per cell when full ✅ Default 4.2 V (4.05 V in 1.16.2). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_DIV 10.1 Battery 2 voltage divider at board default ✅ Default 10.1 (Cube Orange board default). Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT2_V_EMPTY 3.6 V 3.6 V per cell when empty ✅ Default 3.6 V. Leave at default since there is no BAT2. BAT3_CAPACITY −1 mAh Battery 3 capacity unknown ✅ Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_N_CELLS 0 Cell count unknown ✅ Default 0. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_R_INTERNAL −1 Ω Use the online estimate ✅ Default −1. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_SOURCE −1 Battery 3 disabled ✅ Default −1 (Disabled). Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_V_CHARGED 4.2 V 4.2 V per cell when full ✅ Default 4.2 V (4.05 V in 1.16.2). Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT3_V_EMPTY 3.6 V 3.6 V per cell when empty ✅ Default 3.6 V. Leave at default since there is no BAT3. BAT_AVRG_CURRENT 15 A 15 A expected in-flight current ✅ Default 15 A. Only used to initialize the in-flight average-current estimate, which feeds remaining-flight-time and RTL triggering. BAT_CRIT_THR 0.25 Critical at 25% remaining ❌ Default 0.07. Triggers the critical-battery reaction (land) much earlier, so the Homebrew lands with a healthy reserve (about 3.75 V per cell with the linear 3.6–4.2 V mapping; 3.71 V in 1.16.2 with 4.05 V). Must stay below BAT_LOW_THR and above BAT_EMERGEN_THR. Units are normalized 0–1, not percent. BAT_EMERGEN_THR 0.15 Emergency at 15% remaining ❌ Default 0.05. Immediate-landing level (about 3.69 V per cell with the linear 3.6–4.2 V mapping; 3.67 V in 1.16.2). Must stay below BAT_CRIT_THR. BAT_LOW_THR 0.35 Low at 35% remaining ❌ Default 0.15. First warning level (about 3.81 V per cell with the linear 3.6–4.2 V mapping; 3.76 V in 1.16.2). Must stay above BAT_CRIT_THR. BAT_V_OFFS_CURR 0 No current-sensor voltage offset ✅ Default 0. Offset in volts, as seen by the ADC input of the current sensor, subtracted before the battery current is computed from the voltage. It was in the 1.16.2 .params template but had no row in the 1.16.2 document and no reason was recorded; the value equals the default, so it is kept as is.

Note that BAT1_V_DIV and BAT1_A_PER_V are calibrated separately for every quadcopter!

On main only batteries 1 and 2 have BAT*_V_DIV, BAT*_A_PER_V and BAT*_V_CHANNEL, so those do not exist for battery 3. BAT*_I_CHANNEL no longer exists for any battery, and BAT*_I_OVERWRITE now exists for all three (in 1.16.2 battery 3 had no BAT3_I_OVERWRITE).

docs.title: CA: Control Allocator
docs.text:
Positions are along the body X and Y axes, in metres, relative to the center of gravity. They describe the physical span of the airframe and are critical to the motor mixer and flight stability. The Generic Quadcopter airframe (4001_quad_x) sets them to ±1 m. The metadata default is 0.

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason CA_ROTOR0_PX 0.25 m Rotor 0 at +0.25 m on X ❌ Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR0_PY 0.25 m Rotor 0 at +0.25 m on Y ❌ Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR1_PX −0.25 m Rotor 1 at −0.25 m on X ❌ Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR1_PY −0.25 m Rotor 1 at −0.25 m on Y ❌ Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR2_PX 0.25 m Rotor 2 at +0.25 m on X ❌ Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR2_PY −0.25 m Rotor 2 at −0.25 m on Y ❌ Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR3_PX −0.25 m Rotor 3 at −0.25 m on X ❌ Default −1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe. CA_ROTOR3_PY 0.25 m Rotor 3 at +0.25 m on Y ❌ Default 1 m (airframe 4001). Physical span of the airframe.

docs.title: COM: Commander
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason COM_ACT_FAIL_ACT 0 Warning only on actuator failure ✅ Default 0 (warning only). The action taken when the failure detector reports a failed actuator (motor); the other options are 1 Hold, 2 Land, 3 Return, and 4 Terminate. It only matters if the actuator failure check is enabled and configured through FD_ACT_EN and the MOTFAIL_* parameters (see the FD and MOTFAIL sections). Max is unsure whether this should be changed to Land (2) since the current sensor is not working, but he uses 0 and it has been fine. COM_ARM_AUTH_MET 0 One-step arming ✅ Default 0 (one arm: request authorization and arm as soon as it is received). The alternative is 1 (two-step arm: the first arm command requests authorization and the second arms if it is authorized). It is only used when COM_ARM_AUTH_REQ is on, so it has no effect here. COM_ARM_AUTH_REQ 0 No arm authorization required ✅ Default 0 (disabled). No authorization is required to arm other than the arm switch. COM_ARM_BAT_MIN 0.50 Refuse to arm below 50% battery ❌ Default −1 (uses BAT_CRIT_THR). Prevents permanently damaging the battery through negligence. 0.50 corresponds to about 3.90 V per cell with the 3.6–4.2 V mapping (3.83 V in 1.16.2), so arming now needs a slightly fuller pack. COM_ARM_CHK_ESCS 0 ESC arming checks disabled ✅ Default 0 (disabled). Enables checks of the ESCs' online status and failures. It is specific to ESCs that report telemetry and must only be enabled if the ESCs support it; these ESCs do not. COM_ARM_HFLT_CHK 0 Disabled; allow arming even if hardfault files are on the SD card ❌ Default 1 (enabled). On main the check also covers watchdog dump files. Enabling means a failed USB connection prevents all further arming until you delete the logs from SD (via the NuttX terminal or taking the SD card out). Super annoying. Still needed on main as of 2026-10-22: PX4 issue #29346 (hardfault of the USB MAVLink task after arming following a USB unplug) is open at the time of writing, and Max reports it affects our board. The issue is filed against the Cube Orange+; its author says it is fixed on main by PRs #28185 and #28197, which was not verified here, so this stays 0 until a test confirms the problem is gone. Trade-off: with the check off the vehicle can arm after an accidental USB disconnect. COM_ARM_MAG_STR 1 Deny arming on a magnetic disturbance ❌ Default 2 (warning only). Controls what happens when the estimator detects a strong magnetic disturbance, as checked according to EKF2_MAG_CHECK: 0 disabled, 1 deny arming, 2 warning only. Denying arming, not just warning, keeps a vehicle with a disturbed magnetometer on the ground. COM_ARM_WO_GPS 0 Deny arming when the GNSS checks fail ❌ Default 1 ("Allow arming (with warning)"; called "Warning only" in 1.16.2). For an autonomous quadcopter, having no usable GPS should stop it from moving forward. These drones only ever fly outdoors. On main, 0 denies arming in all modes when a check enabled in GNSS_CHECK fails (reported as, for example, "Preflight: GPS fix too low"; estimatorCheck.cpp). The 1.16.2 text also said a global position estimate is required, which is why EKF2_HGT_REF must stay 1; that part was not re-checked on main. With GNSS_CHECK = 2047 and GNSS_REQ_FIX = 6 (see the GNSS section) arming is denied unless the receiver reports RTK fixed. COM_ARMABLE 1 Arming allowed ✅ Default 1 (arming allowed). Set it to 0 to prevent arming entirely, for example for safety or maintenance reasons, so the vehicle cannot be used by accident. COM_DISARM_LAND 2.0 s 2.0 s of successful landing detected ✅ Default 2.0 s. PX4 must detect that the vehicle is on the ground for this long before disarming the motors at the end of Land mode procedure. COM_DISARM_PRFLT 10 s Disarm after 10 s without takeoff ✅ Default 10 s. If the vehicle is armed and has not taken off within this time, it disarms again (a negative value disables this). The user has 10 s to act after arming. COM_DL_LOSS_T 5 s GCS connection counted as lost after 5 s ❌ Default 10 s. Tighter is better, and 10 s is too generous, especially for an autonomous quadcopter. Because NAV_DLL_ACT is set as 0 later, this value is ignored, but it's good to have. COM_FAIL_ACT_T 5 s Wait 5 s in Hold before a failsafe action ✅ Default 5 s. Before a failsafe action (Return, Land, or Hold) is executed, PX4 first waits this long in Hold mode so the user can realize something is wrong. During that time the pilot cannot take over with the stick override (MAN_OVERRIDE_SPD), although switching modes is still allowed; afterwards the configured action runs and the stick override works again. A value of 0 removes the delay. From the description it applies to the failsafes that are active here, such as RC loss (NAV_RCL_ACT) and offboard loss (COM_OBL_RC_ACT); the GCS-loss failsafe is disabled (NAV_DLL_ACT = 0), so it never starts this wait (my reading of the description; not tested). The stick-override part comes from the 1.16.2 description (COM_RC_OVERRIDE) and was not re-verified against the failsafe code on main, where the override is now MAN_OVERRIDE_SPD. COM_FLT_TIME_MAX −1 s No maximum flight time ✅ Default −1 (disabled). When set, the vehicle aborts the current operation and returns to launch once the time since takeoff exceeds this value, with a warning every minute starting at 90 % of it. No maximum flight time is used; the battery thresholds limit the flight time instead. COM_FLTMODE1 2 Slot 1: Position ("Position / Cruise" on main) ❌ Default −1 (unassigned). Necessary for using the Taranis QX7 remote specifically. With RC_MAP_FLTMODE the mode is picked by the range channel 5 is in, across six slots. A different RC would need a different scheme. COM_FLTMODE2 1 Slot 2: Altitude ❌ Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTMODE3 4 Slot 3: Hold ❌ Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTMODE4 1 Slot 4: Altitude ❌ Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. Slots 2 and 4 are both Altitude. COM_FLTMODE5 11 Slot 5: Land ❌ Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTMODE6 8 Slot 6: Stabilized ❌ Default −1 (unassigned). Same Taranis QX7 scheme. COM_FLTT_LOW_ACT 1 Warning when remaining flight time is low ✅ Default 1 (Warning) on main; the 1.16.2 default was 3 (Return), which is what this document used to use. The new default is accepted, so a drone that previously returned now only warns. Options: 0 None, 1 Warning, 3 Return. It should hardly ever matter since the Park is so small. What is critical is that the return heights stay below the net, which is covered by RTL_RETURN_ALT and RTL_DESCEND_ALT. COM_HOME_EN 1 Home position set automatically ✅ Default 1 (enabled). PX4 sets the home position automatically when possible (per Max, on arm or boot). Requires reboot. Home cannot be reset without arming, which is one reason the geofence altitude limit is not used (see GF_MAX_VER_DIST). COM_HOME_IN_AIR 0 Home is never set in the air ✅ Default 0 (disabled). If enabled, the autopilot may set its home position after takeoff (back-computed from the local position when one is available). Disabled so that home is never set while flying. COM_LOW_BAT_ACT 2 Land mode ❌ Default 0 (Warning only). Land instead of just warning at critical battery. Option 4 (return at the critical level, terminate at the emergency level) is new on main and not used. COM_OBL_RC_ACT 4 Land mode (on offboard loss) ❌ Default 0 (Position mode). Note: this is the offboard-loss action, not RC loss (see NAV_RCL_ACT). COM_OF_LOSS_T 0.5 0.5 s offboard-loss timeout ❌ Default 1.0 s. Lowering makes crashes less likely during offboard network dropouts since the failsafe triggers faster. Too low may make this sensitive to network lag, but lower than 0.5 should be tested for feasibility. COM_POS_FS_EPH 5 m Failsafe above 5 m horizontal position error ✅ Default 5 m (−1 disables). The horizontal position error (EPH) above which PX4 triggers a failsafe; once the error has been below the threshold, a factor of 2.5 is applied before the position is invalidated. Kept at default because the offboard code should land, or refuse to arm, whenever the GPS fix type is not 6 (RTK fixed), long before PX4's own failsafe matters. COM_POS_LOW_ACT 5 Land on a low position accuracy ❌ Default 3 (Return). The action taken when the position accuracy is worse than the COM_POS_LOW_EPH threshold (0 None, 1 Warning, 2 Hold, 3 Return, 4 Terminate, 5 Land). Set to Land so that a poor position estimate lands the vehicle instead of returning it. Per the v1.16.2 description the action is only executed in Mission or Hold (loiter) modes, and otherwise it is only a warning; while COM_POS_LOW_EPH is disabled it has no effect at all. COM_POS_LOW_EPH −1 m Low accuracy failsafe disabled ✅ Default −1 (disabled). Threshold for COM_POS_LOW_ACT. The local position must still be valid for it to apply, which requires some velocity aiding or a large dead-reckoning time (EKF2_NOAID_TOUT), together with a high COM_POS_FS_EPH. No motivation to change. COM_PREARM_MODE 0 Prearm state disabled ✅ Default 0 (disabled). The prearmed state is an intermediate state between disarmed and armed in which non-throttling actuators are active; the options are 0 disabled, 1 safety button, 2 always. The prearm feature is not used here. Option 1 is labelled "When safety off" on main. COM_RC_IN_MODE 3 RC or MAVLink, keep first ✅ Default is 3 on main and in 1.16.2. Labelled "RC or MAVLink keep first until reboot" on main ("RC or Joystick keep first" in 1.16.2); "Joystick" is now "MAVLink" in the labels, and priority modes 5 to 8 are new. COM_RC_LOSS_T 0.5 s RC counted as lost after 0.5 s without input ✅ Default 0.5 s. Time without a new setpoint from the RC or a joystick after which the connection is considered lost. It must be short, because the vehicle keeps using the last supplied setpoint until the timeout triggers. COM_RCL_EXCEPT 7 Mission, all auto modes, and Offboard ❌ Default 0 (no exceptions). Bitmask to specify where to ignore loss of manual control and not trigger the failsafe specified in NAV_RCL_ACT. The bits changed since 1.16.2: bit 0 Mission, bit 1 "Auto modes" (was Hold only; now Hold, Takeoff, Land, Return, Descend, Follow Target, Precland and Orbit), bit 2 Offboard, and new bits 3 (external mode) and 4 (altitude cruise). Value 7 therefore now also ignores RC loss during Takeoff, Land, Return and the other auto modes, not only Mission, Hold and Offboard. Required for multi-agent setups since we only have one RC, but consider reverting to default when testing single-agent; RC then becomes required again. COM_SPOOLUP_TIME 1.0 s 1.0 s spool-up after arming ✅ Default 1.0 s. The minimum time from arming the motors until the vehicle can be moved: the motors and propellers spool up to idle before being commanded faster, and the ESCs and smart batteries have time for their failure checks. Commands to move the vehicle are not applied until this time has passed after arming. No motivation to change. COM_VEL_FS_EVH 1 m/s Failsafe above 1 m/s horizontal velocity error ✅ Default 1 m/s. The horizontal velocity error (EVH) above which PX4 triggers a failsafe, with the same factor of 2.5 between validating and invalidating as COM_POS_FS_EPH. No motivation to change. COM_WIND_MAX −1 m/s High wind failsafe disabled ✅ Default −1 (disabled). The estimated wind speed above which the action in COM_WIND_MAX_ACT is triggered. No motivation to change; just do not fly in wind. COM_WIND_MAX_ACT 0 No high wind action ✅ Default 0 (None). The action taken at COM_WIND_MAX (1 Warning, 2 Hold, 3 Return, 4 Terminate, 5 Land). No motivation to change. COM_WIND_WARN −1 m/s Wind warning disabled ✅ Default −1 (disabled). When enabled, a warning is sent every minute while the estimated wind speed is above this value. No motivation to change.

docs.title: EKF2: Estimator
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason EKF2_EV_CTRL 0 External vision fusion disabled ✅ Default 0. Only relevant if a motion-capture system outdoors or a computer-vision camera aids the position estimate. This quad and workspace has neither. The sample drone had 15 (all four bits: horizontal position, vertical position, 3D velocity, yaw); Max is surprised by that and does not know who set it. Per the v1.16 source this is not limited to mocap or cameras: it applies to any vision/odometry input PX4 receives (for example MAVLink VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE or ODOMETRY, which a companion computer could send). EKF2_EV_DELAY 0 ms No external vision delay ✅ Default 0 ms. Delay of the external vision estimate relative to the IMU. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. Requires reboot. EKF2_EV_NOISE_MD 0 EV-reported variance ✅ Default 0 (the measurement noise comes from the vision message, with the EV noise parameters as a lower bound; 1 uses the noise parameters directly). Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_POS_X 0.000 m Vision sensor at the CG on X ✅ Default 0.0. Position of the vision sensor focal point in the body frame. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_POS_Y 0.000 m Vision sensor at the CG on Y ✅ Default 0.0. Position of the vision sensor focal point in the body frame. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_POS_Z 0.000 m Vision sensor at the CG on Z ✅ Default 0.0. Position of the vision sensor focal point in the body frame. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EV_QMIN 0 No minimum vision quality ✅ Default 0 (range 0 to 100). Minimum quality metric, an optional field some VIO systems provide, for external vision to be started and fused. Only relevant if a motion-capture system or a computer-vision camera aids PX4 in estimating pose and twist, which this vehicle does not use (EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0); RTK makes such sources likely unnecessary anyway. EKF2_EVV_NOISE 0.1 m/s Vision velocity noise 0.1 m/s ✅ Default 0.1 m/s. Measurement noise for vision velocity measurements, used to lower bound or replace the uncertainty in the message. No motivation to change, and it is not relevant without external vision such as mocap anyway. EKF2_GPS_CTRL 7 Lon/lat + altitude + 3D velocity fusion ✅ Default 7. Dual-antenna heading (bit 3) stays off. Fusion also needs bit 0 of EKF2_SENS_EN (see below). EKF2_HGT_REF 1 GPS is the height reference ✅ Default 1. This was contentious. The Astro's GPS vertical fix is much better than the Homebrew's, so without RTK the Homebrew tends to wander vertically when holding position in Position Mode (e.g., 0.5-1 m). Choosing 2 (range sensor) looks like a fix but makes global_position_invalid always true, so transitions into modes such as Hold are declined. This has the consequene that the drone gets stuck taking off (can never transition to Hold from Takeoff) or that it cannot land when using a ROS 2 teleop node if the code first dictates a transition to Hold mode. Hence: use RTK for better estimates and keep 1 so global_position_invalid stays false. (This is the lab's observation; I have not verified the global_position_invalid behaviour in the PX4 source. The source does say the range-sensor option should only be used over a flat surface, because the local NED origin then moves with ground level.) EKF2_IMU_POS_X 0.0587 m IMU 0.0587 m forward of CG ❌ Default 0.0. Max does not know who set this or where the value came from. EKF2_IMU_POS_Y 0.000 m IMU on centerline ✅ Default 0.0. EKF2_IMU_POS_Z 0.000 m IMU at CG height ✅ Default 0.0. EKF2_MAG_CHECK 1 Magnetic field strength check only ✅ Default 1 (strength only). Bitmask of the checks that decide whether the magnetometer data is valid: bit 0 field strength (tolerance EKF2_MAG_CHK_STR, 0.2 gauss), bit 1 field inclination (EKF2_MAG_CHK_INC, 20 degrees), bit 2 wait for GNSS to provide the theoretical strength and inclination from the World Magnetic Model (WMM). If GNSS data is received the field is compared with the WMM, otherwise with an average value. The check is useful to reject occasional hard-iron disturbances, and with COM_ARM_MAG_STR = 1 a failed check denies arming. Max would enable all the checks (7), but everything works and he has never broken a magnetometer in a crash, so there is no motivation to move away from the default. EKF2_MIN_RNG 0.01 m Expected ground range 0.01 m ✅ Default 0.01 m on main (it became the default in 1.17.0; 1.16.2 had 0.1 m). The range finder reading the estimator assumes when the vehicle is on the ground and not moving, and the range finder returns invalid data or none, for example because it is inside its minimum measurement distance. The terrain estimator then still has a terrain height at the start of flight. Max applied 0.01 m (the lowest allowed value) early on 1.16.2 because he expected it to become the default; that is now confirmed in source. EKF2_MULTI_IMU 3 Run 3 EKFs, one per IMU ❌ Default 0 (disabled). The flight controller has 3 IMUs inside, and letting PX4 pick the best estimate among them is a good idea. Requires SENS_IMU_MODE = 0. Requires reboot. PX4 only rewrites this value itself when it is outside 1 to 4 while SENS_IMU_MODE is 0. EKF2_MULTI_MAG 0 Multi-EKF magnetometers disabled ✅ Default 0 (disabled). Maximum number of magnetometers to use for Multi-EKF; it requires SENS_MAG_MODE = 0 and a reboot. Left disabled because, unlike the IMUs, Max reports that the Cube does not have multiple magnetometers. The Here4 also provides a compass over DroneCAN (UAVCAN_SUB_MAG), so PX4 sees more than one. As far as I can tell, the sensors module chooses between them by priority and health (see the CAL_MAGn_PRIO parameters), not through UAVCAN_ENABLE. Max thinks both are reasonably accurate but is not sure which one is in use. If magnetometer issues appear, this is a good place to start. EKF2_OF_CTRL 1 Optical flow fusion enabled ✅ Default is 1 in v1.16. Kept explicit so flow is always used. Flow data arrives over CAN (see UAVCAN_SUB_FLOW). Must match bit 2 of EKF2_SENS_EN: a source is fused only if its EKF2_SENS_EN bit and its own control parameter are both nonzero. EKF2_OF_POS_X 0.04440 m Flow sensor 0.0444 m forward of CG ❌ Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_OF_POS_Y 0.06670 m Flow sensor 0.0667 m right of CG ❌ Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_OF_POS_Z 0.05080 m Flow sensor 0.0508 m below CG ❌ Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_RNG_A_HMAX 5.0 m Range aid up to 5.0 m height ✅ Default 5.0 m (range 1 to 10). Maximum height above ground for the conditional range aid (EKF2_RNG_CTRL = 1): above it the estimator stops fusing the range finder for height. EKF2_RNG_A_VMAX 1.0 m/s Range aid up to 1.0 m/s horizontal speed ✅ Default 1.0 m/s (range 0.1 to 2). Maximum horizontal speed for the conditional range aid (EKF2_RNG_CTRL = 1): above it the estimator stops fusing the range finder for height. EKF2_RNG_CTRL 1 Range finder enabled (conditional mode) ✅ Default 1. Range aiding is used at low speed and low altitude (takeoff/landing). Must match bit 9 of EKF2_SENS_EN (this parameter must stay 1 or 2 while that bit is set). EKF2_RNG_POS_X −0.00635 m Rangefinder 0.00635 m behind CG ❌ Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_RNG_POS_Y 0.0539 m Rangefinder 0.0539 m right of CG ❌ Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_RNG_POS_Z 0.114 m Rangefinder 0.114 m below CG ❌ Default 0.0. Sensor mounting offset. EKF2_SENS_EN 1797 GNSS 0, optical flow, barometer, range finder, magnetometer ❌ Default 8191 (all 13 sources). New on main: a bitmask of which sensor fusion sources are enabled, applied only while disarmed (EKF2::initFusionControl(); in flight use the MAVLink command or the individual *_CTRL parameters). A source is fused only if both its EKF2_SENS_EN bit and its own control parameter are nonzero (intended() = enabled && available, where available comes from EKF2_GPS_CTRL, EKF2_OF_CTRL, EKF2_RNG_CTRL, EKF2_BARO_CTRL, EKF2_MAG_TYPE and so on), so a mismatch silently disables a source. Bit map below. Value 1797 = 0b0011100000101. Not 1798: that string (0b0011100000110) clears bit 0 (GNSS 0 off) and sets bit 1 (GNSS 1 on).

docs.title: EKF2_SENS_EN bit map for the Homebrew
docs.text:
Bit numbers and names are from the main module.yaml and the SensEn enum in EKF2.hpp.

Bit Source Set Why 0 GNSS 0 1 The Here4. EKF2_GPS_CTRL is 7, so it matches. 1 GNSS 1 0 There is no second GPS and we do not want PX4 to think there is one. That GPS still loads and works with this bit off needs an in-person test. 2 Optical flow 1 Must match EKF2_OF_CTRL (1). 3 External vision 0 RTK is good enough that feeding PX4 e.g. on-board computer vision would only confuse it, and the Park has no mocap. Matches EKF2_EV_CTRL = 0. 4 to 7 Aux global position 0 to 3 0 Nothing like this on the vehicle. 8 Barometer 1 Very important source of height estimates. EKF2_BARO_CTRL is at its default of 1. 9 Range finder 1 Must match EKF2_RNG_CTRL being enabled (1 or 2). It is 1. 10 Magnetometer 1 Critical for estimation. EKF2_MAG_TYPE is at its default (Automatic). 11 Airspeed 0 Quadcopters, no airspeed sensor. 12 Ranging beacon 0 No ranging beacon.

Bits 0, 2, 8, 9 and 10 set: 1 + 4 + 256 + 512 + 1024 = 1797.

Max is not fully sure how this bitmask should be matched with EKF2_OF_CTRL and EKF2_RNG_CTRL. The source shows the AND behaviour described above, but how it plays out on the real vehicle is exactly what the test flight is for.

docs.title: FD: Failure Detector
docs.text:
The actuator (motor) failure check moved into the ESC arming checks on main (escCheck.cpp). Its parameters were replaced: FD_ACT_MOT_C2T, FD_ACT_MOT_THR and FD_ACT_MOT_TOUT no longer exist and are superseded by MOTFAIL_C2T, MOTFAIL_OFF and MOTFAIL_TIME (no value migration). FD_ACT_EN still exists, but its default flipped from 1 to 0. Everything here stays at its default. Per the main description the check only works for ESCs that report current consumption; the notes for COM_ARM_CHK_ESCS say these ESCs do not, so with the check enabled it would be inert at best.

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason FD_ACT_EN 0 Actuator failure check disabled ✅ Default 0 (disabled) on main; it was 1 in 1.16.2. If enabled, the HealthAndArmingChecks verify that each motor draws a minimum ESC current per throttle level, otherwise this indicates a motor failure. Leave at default.

docs.title: GF: Geofence
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason GF_ACTION 5 Land mode on geofence violation ❌ Default 2 (Hold mode). Land immediately rather than hover. GF_MAX_VER_DIST 0 m Disabled ✅ Default 0 (disabled). Do not use this feature. Because the GPS fix moves during the 1-10 minute initial RTK fix, the relative altitude (relative to the fix when it first boots) will make the quadcopter think it's all over the place. Since you cannot reset the home position without arming, using this feature to prevent the quadcopter from hitting the net as an extra safety feature is moot. Just use CBFs. This feature would interfere with CBF offboard code anyways. If not using RTK (you should really just use it), the estimates are likely not good enough to prevent you from hitting the net. And, PX4's geofence does not take into account for instance the speed at which you approach a geofence, so it's not even enforceable as a never-cross-this boundary.

docs.title: GNSS: GNSS Quality Requirements
docs.text:
New on main. The receiver selection, the per-receiver antenna offsets and delays (SENS_GNSS0_*, see the SENS section) and the quality checks moved from EKF2 to the sensors module (vehicle_gps_position). The GNSS_REQ_* thresholds are the "strict" checks that qualify a receiver, mainly before arming. Once the strict checks have passed on the ground, the checks that decide while armed are the "relaxed" ones with fixed limits: at least a 3D fix, at most 50 m position accuracy and 10 m/s speed accuracy (gnss_checks.cpp). They replace EKF2_GPS_CHECK and EKF2_REQ_*. GNSS_REQ_TIME (default 10 s, the continuous healthy time required at startup) is new too and is left at its default.

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason GNSS_CHECK 2047 All checks except jamming ✅ Default 2047 (range 0 to 4095). Replaces EKF2_GPS_CHECK (1023 in 1.16.2, bits 0 to 9). Bits: 0 satellite count, 1 PDOP, 2 EPH, 3 EPV, 4 speed accuracy, 5 horizontal position drift, 6 vertical position drift, 7 horizontal speed offset, 8 vertical speed offset, 9 spoofing, 10 GNSS fix type (new), 11 jamming (off). The automatic migration would carry 1023 over, which leaves bit 10 off and GNSS_REQ_FIX unenforced, so 2047 is set explicitly. Most 1.16.2 tests were done with 245 and without RTK, because Max did not yet know what he was doing. GNSS_REQ_EPH 3.0 m Maximum 3.0 m horizontal position error to use GNSS ✅ Default 3.0 m (range 0.1 to 100; it was 2 to 100 as EKF2_REQ_EPH). Replaces EKF2_REQ_EPH. Maximum horizontal position error (EPH) the receiver may report (bit 2 of GNSS_CHECK). On its own this threshold does not require RTK; GNSS_REQ_FIX does. GNSS_REQ_EPV 5.0 m Maximum 5.0 m vertical position error to use GNSS ✅ Default 5.0 m (range 0.1 to 100; 2 to 100 as EKF2_REQ_EPV). Replaces EKF2_REQ_EPV. Maximum vertical position error (EPV) the receiver may report (bit 3 of GNSS_CHECK). GNSS_REQ_FIX 6 RTK fixed required ❌ Default 3 (3D fix). New on main, no 1.16.2 equivalent. Values: 0 none, 2 2D, 3 3D, 4 RTCM code differential, 5 RTK float, 6 RTK fixed, 8 extrapolated. The strict check fails when the reported fix type is below this value (gnss_checks.cpp) and only runs if bit 10 of GNSS_CHECK is set. Max set 6 so that nobody flies without RTK any more: with COM_ARM_WO_GPS = 0 arming is denied unless the receiver reports RTK fixed. Scope: this is a strict check. While armed, only the relaxed checks decide (3D fix minimum), so losing RTK in flight does not by itself trip it; the offboard code should still land when the fix type drops below 6, as before. GNSS_REQ_HDRIFT 0.1 m/s Maximum 0.1 m/s horizontal drift to use GNSS ✅ Default 0.1 m/s (range 0.1 to 1.0, so this is also the strictest allowed value). Replaces EKF2_REQ_HDRIFT. Used for the horizontal position drift and horizontal speed offset checks (bits 5 and 7 of GNSS_CHECK), which only run when the vehicle is on the ground and stationary. GNSS_REQ_NSATS 6 At least 6 satellites to use GNSS ✅ Default 6 (range 4 to 12). Replaces EKF2_REQ_NSATS. Minimum satellite count (bit 0 of GNSS_CHECK). GNSS_REQ_PDOP 2.5 Maximum PDOP 2.5 to use GNSS ✅ Default 2.5 (range 1.5 to 5.0). Replaces EKF2_REQ_PDOP. Maximum position dilution of precision (bit 1 of GNSS_CHECK). GNSS_REQ_SACC 0.5 m/s Maximum 0.5 m/s speed accuracy to use GNSS ✅ Default 0.5 m/s (range 0.5 to 5.0, so this is also the strictest allowed value). Replaces EKF2_REQ_SACC. Maximum speed accuracy (bit 4 of GNSS_CHECK). Per the main description, EKF2 also uses this limit for feeding GNSS velocity to the EKF-GSF yaw estimator and for trusting GNSS vertical velocity while the accelerometer clips, in flight too. No motivation to change. GNSS_REQ_VDRIFT 0.2 m/s Maximum 0.2 m/s vertical drift to use GNSS ✅ Default 0.2 m/s (range 0.1 to 1.5). Replaces EKF2_REQ_VDRIFT. Used for the vertical position drift and vertical speed offset checks (bits 6 and 8 of GNSS_CHECK), which only run when the vehicle is on the ground and stationary.

docs.title: GPS: Serial GPS
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason GPS_1_CONFIG 0 Serial GPS driver disabled ❌ Default 201 (GPS 1). The GPS is the Here4 on DroneCAN, so the serial GPS driver stays off.

docs.title: MAN: Manual Control
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason MAN_ARM_GESTURE 0 Stick arm/disarm gesture disabled ❌ Default 1 (enabled). Prevents accidental arming/disarming by stick position. MAN_KILL_GEST_T −1 Kill stick gesture disabled ✅ Default −1 (negative value disables the feature). MAN_OVERRIDE_SPD 1.0 /s Stick override on, 1.0 stick travel per second ✅ Default 1.0 (range -1 to 10; negative disables). Replaces COM_RC_OVERRIDE (3 in 1.16.2: auto and offboard modes) and COM_RC_STICK_OV (30 %). In auto and offboard modes, on a multicopter, the pilot takes over (Position mode, or Altitude if position is unavailable) when any of the four sticks moves faster than this threshold for several consecutive samples (ManualControl.cpp, Commander::manualControlCheck()). It measures stick speed in stick travel per second, not a 30 % displacement, so the sensitivity is not equivalent to the old setting; Max accepted the default. It is considered more important than stick nudging (see MPC_AUTO_NUDGING).

docs.title: MAV: MAVLink
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason MAV_0_CONFIG 101 MAVLink instance 0 on TELEM 1 ✅ Default 101 (TELEM 1). The QGC telemetry radio connects here. Requires reboot. If torque-level control is ever wanted, note that (per Max, not verified by me) MAVROS does not support torque-level commands but uXRCE-DDS does, while RTK is not possible over uXRCE-DDS on main because there is no topic for it yet. The open PR #29368 (the branch under test on 2026-10-22, not merged) adds /fmu/in/rtcm_corrections (px4_msgs/msg/RtcmData) to the uXRCE-DDS client, which would remove the need to run MAVROS next to it for RTK. Torque-level control plus RTK would therefore need uXRCE-DDS and MAVROS running together. That would need a third serial port, because TELEM 1 and TELEM 2 are taken by the QGC radio and the Jetson link, and giving up the QGC radio is extremely dangerous for a torque-level offboard flight. Options are to wait until uXRCE-DDS supports RTK or MAVROS supports torque-level control, to write custom PX4 topics for RTK over uXRCE-DDS, or to solder a new cable and run uXRCE-DDS on another port such as GPS 2 (not tried). MAV_1_CONFIG 102 MAVLink instance 1 on TELEM 2 ❌ Default 0 (disabled). The FTDI-to-USB cable to the Jetson connects to the flight controller here. Requires reboot. MAV_1_FLOW_CTRL 2 Serial flow control auto-detected ✅ Default 2. The Jetson link. This setting tells PX4 to auto-detect flow control; PX4 does not write the parameter itself. Use 0 or 1 only if auto-detection fails. Requires reboot. MAV_1_FORWARD 0 No message forwarding from the Jetson link ✅ Default 0. Broadcast messages (or ones aimed at another system) arriving on the Jetson link are not forwarded to the other MAVLink links. Requires reboot. MAV_1_MODE 2 Onboard message set ✅ Default 2 (Onboard). The set of streamed messages on the Jetson link is the one meant for a companion computer. Requires reboot. MAV_1_RATE 0 B/s Rate limit chosen from the baud rate ✅ Default 0. With 0, PX4 uses half the theoretical bandwidth, baud/20 bytes per second; at 921600 baud that is 46080 B/s. PX4 does not write the parameter itself. Requires reboot. MAV_PROTO_VER 2 Always use MAVLink 2 ✅ Default is 2 on main (it was 0 in 1.16.2: start with MAVLink 1 and switch to 2 if the GCS sends version 2). Option 0 no longer exists; option 1 is now "Version 1 with auto-upgrade to v2 if detected". Not super critical. MAV_SYS_ID TBD (2–249) Unique number per homebrew vehicle ❌ Default 1. Never use 1 (every Astro requires 1 and it can't be changed). Choosing 1 will cause ROS 2 topic to intermingle between the Astro and Homebrew despite being namespaced. Must be unique. Range 1–250; never pick 250. Requires reboot. MAV_TYPE 2 Quadrotor ✅ MC default 2 (metadata 0, generic micro air vehicle, overridden by rc.mc_defaults). The airframe type announced over MAVLink. Not super critical.

docs.title: MC: Multicopter Autotune
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason MC_AT_EN 1 Autotune module enabled ❌ Default 0 (disabled). Allows autotuning the control cascade from QGC. This does not mean the quad tunes continuously in flight. Do not run it unless there is a reason to suspect poor control performance, which there really should not be.

docs.title: MIS: Mission
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT 2.5 m Take off to 2.5 m from ground level ✅ Default 2.5 m. Take off to 2.5 m from ground level

docs.title: MOTFAIL: Motor Failure
docs.text:
Replacement parameters for FD_ACT_MOT_*. All stay at their defaults and are inert while FD_ACT_EN is 0. The main descriptions of these three still mention the old FD_ACT_* names, so read them with that in mind.

Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason MOTFAIL_C2T 35 A/% Current-to-throttle scale 35 A/% ✅ Default 35 (range 0 to 50). The slope between the expected steady-state current and the linearized, normalized thrust command. The old FD_ACT_MOT_C2T default was 2, so the number is not comparable. Leave at default. MOTFAIL_OFF 10 A Over/under-current offset 10 A ✅ Default 10 A (range 0 to 30). The check triggers if the difference between the expected and measured current is above this value. Leave at default. MOTFAIL_TIME 1.0 s Violation must last 1.0 s ✅ Default 1.0 s (range 0.01 to 10). The current thresholds must be exceeded for this long before a motor failure triggers. The old FD_ACT_MOT_TOUT was in milliseconds (default 100). Leave at default.

docs.title: MPC: Multicopter Position Control
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason MPC_AUTO_NUDGING 0 Stick nudging in auto modes disabled ✅ Default 0. Replaces MPC_LAND_RC_HELP (0 in 1.16.2, so nothing is lost; a nonzero old value would have migrated to bit 1). Bitmask: bit 0 yaw nudging in all auto modes, bit 1 landing nudging (pitch/roll move the vehicle horizontally, the throttle stick scales the descent speed from 0 to 2 times MPC_LAND_SPEED, yaw rotates the heading). Deliberately left off: the main description says stick override must be disabled (MAN_OVERRIDE_SPD = -1) for nudging to work, and Commander::manualControlCheck() has no exception for nudging, so the two are mutually exclusive in practice. Max prefers the override. Other points from the 1.16.2 reasoning that still apply if this is ever enabled: the throttle stick on a Taranis QX7 does not spring back to center, so an RC left on with throttle low would double the descent speed of every Land, including a battery failsafe Land (COM_LOW_BAT_ACT) (my inference from the description), and it has no effect in Offboard. MPC_LAND_RADIUS, which limits how far landing nudging can move the quad, now defaults to -1 (no limit); it was 1000 m in 1.16.2.

docs.title: NAV: Navigator
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason NAV_DLL_ACT 0 Disabled (no GCS-loss failsafe) ✅ Default 0. Removes the need for QGC to stay connected. Required for multi-agent setups. NAV_RCL_ACT 3 Land mode on RC loss ❌ Default 2 (Return mode). Land in place instead of returning. Option 7 ("Hold mode (no failsafe)") is new on main and not used.

docs.title: PLD: Precision Landing
docs.text: Parameter Name Setting (Raw) Setting (Word) Is Default (MC) Reason PLD_SRCH_ALT 2.5 m Climb to 2.5 m above home when searching for the landing target ❌ Default 10 m. Our flight space has a net at 8 m.

docs.title: PWM: Motor Outputs
docs.text:
These are what the motors for this quadcopter need. Output functions 101 to 104 are Motor 1 to Motor 4.
